description: Transform AgentBio Intelligence from a functional MVP into an enterprise-grade, production-ready real estate SaaS platform. Covers CI/CD, testing, security hardening, compliance, monitoring, performance, and code quality — systematically closing every gap identified in the production readiness audit.

userStories.title: Configure ESLint and Prettier for consistent code quality
userStories.description: As a developer, I need automated code linting and formatting so that all contributions follow consistent standards and common bugs are caught early.
acceptanceCriteria: Install eslint, @typescript-eslint/parser, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin, eslint-plugin-react, eslint-plugin-react-hooks, prettier, eslint-config-prettier
Create .eslintrc.cjs with TypeScript strict rules, React hooks rules, and import ordering
Create .prettierrc with singleQuote: true, semi: true, trailingComma: 'es5', printWidth: 100, tabWidth: 2
Add 'lint' and 'format' scripts to package.json
Running 'npm run lint' completes without crashing (warnings are acceptable for existing code, no new errors introduced)
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Do NOT auto-fix existing code in this story. Only set up the tooling. Existing violations will be addressed incrementally.

userStories.title: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged
userStories.description: As a developer, I need pre-commit hooks that automatically lint and format staged files so that broken or inconsistent code never enters the repository.
acceptanceCriteria: Install husky and lint-staged as devDependencies
Configure husky with a pre-commit hook that runs lint-staged
lint-staged config: run eslint --fix and prettier --write on staged .ts/.tsx files
Add 'prepare' script to package.json: 'husky'
Creating a test commit with a staged .ts file triggers the hook successfully
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (ESLint/Prettier must be configured first).

userStories.title: Create GitHub Actions CI workflow for type checking and build verification
userStories.description: As a developer, I need automated CI checks on every pull request so that type errors and build failures are caught before merge.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml triggered on push to main and on pull_request
Job 1: 'typecheck' — runs tsc --noEmit on Node 20
Job 2: 'build' — runs npm run build, fails if build errors occur
Both jobs use npm ci for deterministic installs
Both jobs cache node_modules using actions/cache with package-lock.json hash
Workflow file is valid YAML (use actionlint or manual validation)
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds locally
userStories.notes: This is the most critical infrastructure gap. The .github/workflows/ directory currently exists but is empty.

userStories.title: Add automated test execution to CI pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tests to run automatically in CI so that regressions are caught on every pull request.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'test' job to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs after typecheck passes
Job runs 'npm run test:run' (vitest in non-watch mode)
Job uploads coverage report as an artifact
Test job uses same Node 20 and npm ci caching pattern
If any existing tests fail, fix them so CI passes green
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Currently 4 test files exist: analytics.test.ts, lead-scoring.test.ts, ml-lead-scoring.test.ts, useMLLeadScoring.test.ts. All must pass.

userStories.title: Add security and dependency audit to CI pipeline
userStories.description: As a security-conscious developer, I need automated vulnerability scanning in CI so that known dependency vulnerabilities are flagged before deployment.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'security' job to .github/workflows/ci.yml
Job runs 'npm audit --audit-level=high' — fails on high/critical vulnerabilities
Job runs the existing lint script if available
Add Dependabot auto-merge for patch updates in .github/dependabot.yml (file may already exist — update it)
Document any existing high/critical vulnerabilities found in a SECURITY_NOTES.md file if they cannot be resolved immediately
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: A dependabot.yml may already exist. Check before creating.

userStories.title: Create comprehensive test utilities and component test helpers
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a test utility module with render helpers, mock providers, and common fixtures so that writing component tests is fast and consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/test/test-utils.tsx that exports a custom render function wrapping components in required providers (QueryClientProvider, BrowserRouter, etc.)
Create src/test/mocks/supabase.ts with a mock Supabase client that stubs auth, from(), storage
Create src/test/mocks/auth.ts with mock user objects (authenticated user, unauthenticated, admin)
Create src/test/fixtures/profile.ts with sample profile data matching the profiles table schema
Create src/test/fixtures/listing.ts with sample listing data
Create src/test/fixtures/lead.ts with sample lead data
Existing tests in src/lib/*.test.ts still pass after changes
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: src/test/setup.ts already exists with basic mocks (matchMedia, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver). Build on that foundation.

userStories.title: Add unit tests for core utility libraries
userStories.description: As a developer, I need thorough unit tests for critical utility modules so that core business logic has verified correctness.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/lib/errorHandler.test.ts — test captureException, handleApiError, sanitization of sensitive data
Create src/lib/logger.test.ts — test log levels, PII redaction (passwords, tokens, emails), environment-aware behavior
Create src/lib/encryption.test.ts — test encrypt/decrypt round-trip, handling of empty strings and special characters
Create src/lib/seo.test.ts — test meta tag generation, slug creation, canonical URL building
All new tests pass with 'npm run test:run'
Combined test coverage for src/lib/ reaches at least 40%
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Focus on testing pure functions and utilities — these are the easiest to test and highest value.

userStories.title: Add component tests for core UI components
userStories.description: As a developer, I need component tests for foundational UI components so that visual regressions and interaction bugs are caught automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Create tests for at least 5 core UI components from src/components/ui/ (e.g., button, input, dialog, select, toast)
Tests verify rendering, user interaction (click, type, select), accessibility attributes (role, aria-label)
Tests use the custom render helper from src/test/test-utils.tsx
Tests use @testing-library/react for queries (getByRole, getByText, etc.)
All tests pass with 'npm run test:run'
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: UI components are built on Radix UI primitives. Test the composed behavior, not Radix internals.

userStories.title: Add component tests for authentication flow
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tests covering login, registration, and auth guards so that authentication—the most security-critical flow—is verified.
acceptanceCriteria: Create tests for the login page component — renders form, validates inputs, handles submit, shows errors
Create tests for the registration page component — renders form, validates inputs, handles submit
Create tests for the ProtectedRoute component — redirects unauthenticated users, renders for authenticated users
Mock Supabase auth methods (signInWithPassword, signUp, getSession) using the mock from src/test/mocks/supabase.ts
All tests pass with 'npm run test:run'
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Auth pages may be in src/pages/auth/. Check App.tsx for route definitions and component imports.

userStories.title: Add hook tests for critical custom hooks
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tests for core custom hooks so that data fetching, state management, and side effects are verified.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/hooks/useProfile.test.ts — test profile fetching, caching, error states
Create src/hooks/useListings.test.ts — test CRUD operations, query invalidation
Create src/hooks/useLeads.test.ts — test lead fetching, status updates
Use @testing-library/react renderHook for all hook tests
Mock Supabase responses for each test scenario (success, error, empty)
All tests pass with 'npm run test:run'
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: These hooks use TanStack Query. Wrap renderHook in a QueryClientProvider with a fresh QueryClient per test.

userStories.title: Enforce test coverage thresholds in CI
userStories.description: As a tech lead, I need minimum test coverage thresholds enforced in CI so that coverage does not regress as the codebase grows.
acceptanceCriteria: Configure vitest.config.ts with coverage thresholds: lines: 15, functions: 15, branches: 15, statements: 15
Update the CI test job to run 'npm run test:coverage' instead of 'npm run test:run'
CI fails if coverage drops below thresholds
Document the current coverage baseline in a comment in vitest.config.ts
All existing tests pass with coverage enabled
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Starting thresholds are deliberately low (15%) to avoid blocking development. Increase incrementally as more tests are added.

userStories.title: Implement centralized API rate limiting for edge functions
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need rate limiting on all public API endpoints so that the system is protected from abuse and DDoS attacks.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a SQL migration adding a rate_limits table: id, ip_address, endpoint, request_count, window_start, created_at
Add indexes on (ip_address, endpoint, window_start) for fast lookups
Create supabase/functions/_shared/rate-limiter.ts utility that checks rate limits using the rate_limits table
Rate limiter supports configurable limits per endpoint (e.g., 60 requests/minute for general, 5/minute for auth)
Rate limiter returns 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header when limit exceeded
Add rate limiting to at least 3 public-facing edge functions (submit-lead, submit-contact, and one auth function)
Typecheck passes on edge function code
userStories.notes: Current rate limiting is in-memory only and does not persist across function instances. Database-backed approach scales.

userStories.title: Create audit logging database schema and trigger system
userStories.description: As a compliance officer, I need an audit log of all significant user and admin actions so that we can investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: Create SQL migration with audit_logs table: id (uuid), user_id (uuid nullable), action (text), resource_type (text), resource_id (uuid nullable), details (jsonb), ip_address (inet), user_agent (text), created_at (timestamptz)
Add index on (user_id, created_at) and (resource_type, resource_id)
Enable RLS: admins can read all logs, users can read only their own logs
Create a reusable SQL function log_audit_event(user_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, details) that inserts into audit_logs
Add triggers on profiles, listings, and leads tables for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE that call log_audit_event
Create a partition strategy comment (partition by month when table grows)
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: This is a compliance blocker for enterprise customers. The audit_logs table is the foundation for SOC 2 and GDPR compliance.

userStories.title: Create audit logging edge function and frontend integration
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an edge function for recording audit events from the frontend so that client-side actions (login, logout, settings changes) are logged.
acceptanceCriteria: Create supabase/functions/audit-log/index.ts edge function (or update if it exists) that accepts {action, resource_type, resource_id, details} and inserts into audit_logs with user context from JWT
Create src/lib/audit.ts client utility with logAuditEvent(action, resourceType, resourceId, details) function
Integrate audit logging into login success, logout, profile update, and listing create/update/delete flows
Audit events include relevant context (what changed, old/new values for updates)
All audit log calls are fire-and-forget (do not block the UI if logging fails)
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: The edge function may already exist at supabase/functions/audit-log/. Check and update rather than recreate.

userStories.title: Implement PII encryption utilities for sensitive data at rest
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need client-side encryption for PII fields so that sensitive data (phone numbers, addresses) is encrypted in the database.
acceptanceCriteria: Review and enhance src/lib/encryption.ts — ensure it uses AES-256-GCM with a proper key derivation from environment variable
Create src/lib/pii.ts with encryptPII(plaintext) and decryptPII(ciphertext) functions that wrap the encryption library
Add VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env.example with documentation
PII functions handle edge cases: null, undefined, empty string (return as-is)
Add unit tests in src/lib/pii.test.ts: encrypt/decrypt round-trip, null handling, different data types
Tests pass with 'npm run test:run'
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: An encryption.ts already exists in src/lib/. Review it first and build on what's there. Key management in production should use Supabase Vault, but env var is acceptable for now.

userStories.title: Apply PII encryption to leads and profiles tables
userStories.description: As a data protection officer, I need phone numbers, addresses, and other PII encrypted at rest so that a database breach does not expose customer data.
acceptanceCriteria: Update the leads hook (src/hooks/useLeads.ts) to encrypt phone and email fields before insert/update using pii.ts
Update the leads hook to decrypt phone and email fields after fetch
Update the profile hook (src/hooks/useProfile.ts) to encrypt phone_number field before save and decrypt after fetch
Create a SQL migration adding encrypted_phone and encrypted_email columns to leads table (keep original columns during migration period)
Add a migration note explaining the transition strategy: encrypt new data, backfill existing data separately
Existing functionality is not broken — forms still display decrypted values
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: This is a gradual migration. Do NOT delete original plaintext columns in this story. A separate backfill + column swap will happen later.

userStories.title: Add React Error Boundaries for all major route sections
userStories.description: As a user, I need graceful error recovery instead of white screens so that a crash in one section does not take down the entire application.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/components/ui/error-boundary.tsx — a reusable ErrorBoundary component with fallback UI showing error message and 'Try Again' button
ErrorBoundary logs errors to errorHandler.captureException and logger.error
ErrorBoundary fallback UI is styled with Tailwind, includes the AgentBio branding, and offers navigation back to dashboard
Wrap each major route section in App.tsx with ErrorBoundary: dashboard routes, auth routes, admin routes, public profile routes
Existing lazy-loaded components wrapped in Suspense+ErrorBoundary pattern
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: A LazyLoadErrorBoundary may already exist. Check first and consolidate into one reusable component.

userStories.title: Standardize error responses across all edge functions
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I need consistent error response formats from all API endpoints so that error handling is predictable and user-friendly.
acceptanceCriteria: Create supabase/functions/_shared/response.ts with helpers: successResponse(data, status?), errorResponse(message, code, status?), validationError(errors)
Response format: {success: boolean, data?: any, error?: {code: string, message: string, details?: any}}
Error codes follow pattern: RESOURCE_ACTION_REASON (e.g., LEAD_CREATE_VALIDATION, AUTH_LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED)
Update at least 10 edge functions to use the standardized response helpers
Document all error codes in a comment block at the top of response.ts
Typecheck passes on edge function code
userStories.notes: A _shared/ directory already exists in supabase/functions/. Check what utilities are already there.

userStories.title: Implement GDPR data export endpoint
userStories.description: As a user, I need to export all my personal data in a machine-readable format so that the platform complies with GDPR Article 20 (right to data portability).
acceptanceCriteria: Create supabase/functions/gdpr-export/index.ts that exports all user data as JSON
Export includes: profile, listings, leads, links, analytics, testimonials, blog posts, and any other user-owned data
Endpoint requires authentication (valid JWT)
Response is a JSON file with Content-Disposition: attachment header
PII fields are decrypted before export (use pii.ts decrypt utilities)
Add rate limiting: max 1 export per hour per user
Log the export event to audit_logs
Typecheck passes on edge function code
userStories.notes: GDPR compliance is a legal requirement for serving EU users. This is a blocker for enterprise sales.

userStories.title: Implement GDPR data deletion endpoint
userStories.description: As a user, I need to request deletion of all my personal data so that the platform complies with GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure).
acceptanceCriteria: Create supabase/functions/gdpr-delete/index.ts that soft-deletes all user data
Deletion covers: profile (anonymize), listings (soft-delete), leads (soft-delete), links (delete), analytics (anonymize), testimonials (soft-delete)
User account is deactivated but auth record retained for 30 days (to prevent re-registration abuse)
Endpoint requires authentication and a confirmation token (sent via email or passed as parameter)
Log the deletion request to audit_logs (with anonymized user reference)
Create a corresponding frontend page at /dashboard/settings/delete-account with confirmation flow
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Soft-delete with 30-day retention is standard practice. Full purge can be a separate scheduled job.

userStories.title: Create Terms of Service page
userStories.description: As a legal stakeholder, I need a Terms of Service page so that the platform has clear legal terms governing its use.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/pages/legal/TermsOfService.tsx with comprehensive ToS content
Content covers: account terms, acceptable use, intellectual property, payment terms, limitation of liability, termination, governing law
Page is styled consistently with existing pages using Tailwind
Add route /terms in App.tsx (public, no auth required)
Add link to Terms in the site footer component
Add last updated date header
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Content should be specific to AgentBio's real estate SaaS context. Include sections about listing data accuracy and lead data handling.

userStories.title: Create Privacy Policy page

acceptanceCriteria: Create src/pages/legal/PrivacyPolicy.tsx with comprehensive privacy policy content

Content covers: data collected (profile, listings, leads, analytics), how data is used, third-party sharing, cookies, data retention, user rights (access, deletion, portability), security measures, contact information
Includes GDPR-specific sections (legal basis, DPO contact, EU user rights)
Includes CCPA-specific sections (California user rights, do not sell)
Page styled consistently with Tailwind
Add route /privacy in App.tsx (public, no auth required)
Add link in site footer
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Check if legal pages directory already exists at src/pages/legal/. Build on existing structure.

userStories.title: Create Cookie Policy page and consent banner

acceptanceCriteria: Create src/pages/legal/CookiePolicy.tsx listing all cookies used (session, analytics, preferences)
Create src/components/ui/cookie-consent.tsx banner component that appears on first visit
Banner offers: Accept All, Reject Non-Essential, Manage Preferences
Store consent choice in localStorage with timestamp
Only initialize Google Analytics if analytics consent is given
Add route /cookies in App.tsx
Add CookieConsent component to App.tsx (renders globally)
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Cookie consent state should be checked before loading any analytics/tracking scripts.

userStories.title: Implement Web Vitals monitoring and reporting
userStories.description: As a performance engineer, I need Core Web Vitals tracking so that we can monitor and optimize LCP, FID, CLS, and TTFB in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Install web-vitals package
Create src/lib/web-vitals.ts that captures LCP, FID, CLS, TTFB, and INP metrics
Report metrics to Google Analytics as custom events (use existing GA integration)
Report metrics to console in development mode for debugging

Log a warning when metrics exceed budgets in development
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Web Vitals are Google's official page experience metrics and affect SEO ranking.

userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need Sentry properly configured with alerting thresholds so that production errors and performance regressions are detected and escalated.
acceptanceCriteria: Review and update src/lib/sentry.ts — ensure performance monitoring sample rate is at least 10% in production

Configure Sentry breadcrumbs for navigation, console, fetch, and DOM events
Add Sentry.captureMessage for critical business events: subscription created, subscription cancelled, lead scored > 90
Create MONITORING.md documenting: what's tracked, alert thresholds, escalation procedures, dashboard URLs
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: Sentry is already partially integrated (src/lib/sentry.ts exists). Enhance rather than rebuild.

userStories.title: Add bundle analysis and size budgets to build pipeline
userStories.description: As a performance engineer, I need automated bundle size tracking so that we can prevent bundle bloat and maintain fast load times.
acceptanceCriteria: Install rollup-plugin-visualizer as a devDependency

userStories.title: Implement service worker for offline support and caching
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I need the app to work offline for previously visited pages so that I can access my profile and listings without connectivity.
acceptanceCriteria: Install workbox-precaching, workbox-routing, workbox-strategies, and workbox-build as devDependencies
Create public/sw.js (or src/sw.ts compiled to public/) with workbox strategies: CacheFirst for static assets, NetworkFirst for API calls, StaleWhileRevalidate for images
Register the service worker in src/main.tsx with update detection and notification
Precache the app shell (index.html, main JS/CSS bundles)
Cache API responses for profile, listings with 5-minute TTL
Add offline fallback page that displays when network is unavailable
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: PWA manifest already exists at public/manifest.json. IndexedDB offline storage exists at src/lib/offline-storage.ts. Service worker is the missing piece.

userStories.title: Fix critical type safety issues — eliminate high-risk 'as any' casts
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the most dangerous 'as any' type casts removed so that TypeScript can catch bugs in critical code paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all files in src/lib/, src/hooks/, and src/stores/ for 'as any' usage
Fix at least 30 'as any' casts by adding proper type definitions
For Supabase query results, use the generated types from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts
For event handlers, use proper React event types (React.ChangeEvent, React.FormEvent, etc.)

userStories.title: Implement session management and session revocation UI
userStories.description: As a security-conscious user, I need to view and revoke active sessions so that I can secure my account if a device is lost or compromised.
acceptanceCriteria: Create SQL migration for sessions table: id, user_id, device_info (jsonb), ip_address, last_active_at, created_at, revoked_at

Log session revocations to audit_logs

Rate limit MFA verification attempts (max 5 per minute)
Log MFA setup and verification events to audit_logs
Edge function typecheck passes

userStories.description: As a user, I need a UI to set up and use two-factor authentication so that I can protect my account with a second factor.

userStories.title: Add image optimization pipeline with WebP conversion

Integrate with listing image upload flow — call optimize-image after upload

Create playwright-e2e.config.ts for E2E tests (separate from security tests)

userStories.title: Implement email service integration for transactional emails
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need a transactional email service so that users receive welcome emails, lead notifications, and password reset emails.

Create supabase/functions/_shared/email.ts with sendEmail(to, subject, html, text) utility

Create a database trigger on the leads table (INSERT) that invokes the notify-lead function via Supabase webhook or pg_net

userStories.title: Complete console.log to secure logger migration across codebase
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need all console.log/error/warn statements replaced with the secure logger so that sensitive data is never leaked to the browser console in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all files in src/ for console.log, console.error, console.warn, console.info, console.debug usage

No raw console statements remain in src/hooks/, src/stores/, src/pages/, or src/components/ (except src/lib/logger.ts itself)
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06. All 38 raw console statements migrated across 25 files; grep over src/components, src/hooks, src/pages and src/stores now returns zero, which is what the acceptance criterion asks for. eslint no-console is down from 20 to 17, the remainder all in src/lib/ and src/integrations/ (logger.ts itself, sw-cleanup, web-vitals, offline-storage, sentry, the supabase client) which the criterion does not cover and where a raw console is the right call -- those are the low-level modules the logger is built on top of. Mostly scripted, then reviewed call by call rather than trusted: console.log/debug -> logger.debug, console.warn -> logger.warn with the second argument wrapped as a context object (logger.warn takes context, not an error), console.error -> logger.error which does take an error second. Four hand corrections the script got wrong or crudely: the two error boundaries pass three arguments, so errorInfo became { componentStack }; LazyLoadErrorBoundary was passing error.message where the Error itself is more useful; and OptimizedImage/ProgressiveImage were logging a failed image URL at error level with the URL in the error slot, now logger.warn with { src } as context. The script also mis-inserted the import into the middle of a multi-line import in four files -- caught by eslint (4 parsing errors) and fixed. Final: eslint 0 errors / 899 warnings (was 0 / 902), tsc back at the 356 baseline, 274 tests pass, build passes.

acceptanceCriteria: npx tsc --noEmit reports 0 errors

userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-09-01. 143 tsc errors -> 0, and CI is re-gated: the ratchet step is replaced by a plain `npx tsc --noEmit`, the "Intentionally NOT gated on typecheck" carve-out comment is gone, and the test job declares `needs: typecheck` again. `npm run test:run` (298 passed) and `npm run build` both pass.

The story's own prediction held on essentially every file: a hand-written type restating a table hid something real. Roughly forty live defects came out with the backlog. The ones worth knowing about:
- Pricing.tsx sent `priceId.replace('monthly','yearly')` to checkout, so choosing Yearly charged the MONTHLY price. subscription_plans has stripe_price_id_monthly/_yearly and get_stripe_price_id() to choose between them; the hand-written SubscriptionPlan listed 5 of 16 columns and hid all of it. NOT verified against live Stripe — worth a manual checkout test.
- Adding a testimonial from the dashboard always failed: the form is camelCase and went straight into an insert, so it named columns that do not exist and omitted NOT NULL client_name.
- SocialShareDialog threw a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError on open and had never rendered once.
- The listing-description tool's paywall never engaged (isUnlocked vs isLocked), so every visitor got all four descriptions without giving an email; EmailCaptureModal also recorded listingId: undefined on the leads it did get.
- FullProfilePage's JSON-LD Review nodes read author/content, not columns, so every review went to Google as "Anonymous" with no body.
- Four of five web vitals were never reported: onFID was removed in web-vitals v4 and threw into a silent catch before CLS/TTFB/INP registered.
- URL-imported listings discarded every scraped photo.
- The admin user list showed every subscription as "none" (plan vs plan_name).
- CompetitorMatrix ordered by a column that does not exist, so its query always errored into a swallowed catch; its three insight cards could never render anyway, reading five non-columns.
- LinkStack custom_css was passed as {cssText}, which React ignores, so it never applied.
- The leads report exported a Score column of zeroes; ListingsBlock rendered prices as "$$450,000"; QuickActionsDashboard showed every listing as $0.
- About a dozen new Date(nullable) sites rendering the Unix epoch as "1/1/1970" or "over 56 years ago".

FIVE hand-written Profile types existed; there is now one, derived from the generated Row, and the same was done for Listing, Testimonial, Lead, Article, SSOConfig, SubscriptionPlan and the SEO admin panels' rows.

METHOD NOTE for future work of this kind: deriving four admin panels' types in one pass took the count 87 -> 126, because each honest type surfaces its own cluster of nullable-column work. Derive ONE type, drive that file to zero, then move on.

FOUND BUT OUT OF SCOPE, each wants its own story:
(1) The schema has a `lead_scores` table (score, probability, confidence, priority, model_version, feature_importance, keyed by lead_id) and NOTHING in src/ or supabase/functions/ reads or writes it. ML scoring is computed client-side per render and persisted nowhere, so scores cannot be queried or compared over time.
(2) Nothing writes seo_competitor_analysis at all — refreshAnalysis is an explicit stub — so CompetitorKeywordGap in CompetitorMatrix.tsx is a contract a future writer must satisfy, not a shape observed in data.
(3) AddTestimonialModal collects a clientPhoto File that nothing uploads; client_photo stores a URL and is left null.
(4) src/utils/sanitize.ts's sanitizeHtml has no callers; its ALLOWED_ATTR bug was latent, not live.

The 89 originals move verbatim to supabase/migrations/archive/ with a README, one level below the directory `supabase db push` reads, so they are preserved for history but never re-run. Proved equivalent rather than assumed: a normalised pg_dump of the single-pass baseline build is byte-for-byte IDENTICAL to the three-pass build it replaces. 134 tables, 101 functions, 277 policies, 402 indexes, 80 triggers, 2 enums. pg_net is guarded in a DO block on pg_available_extensions rather than dropped: hosted Supabase ships it and notify_lead_on_insert() calls net.http_post(), but a plain Postgres does not, and the unguarded CREATE EXTENSION was one of the ten failures. Checked what the old failure had actually cost — the profiles.notification_preferences column, the function and its trigger all survived, because the old CI loop ran psql without ON_ERROR_STOP and continued past the failing statement; only the extension itself was missing. verify-backend.yml's three-pass loop is now one pass with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 and errors fatal, so a regression fails the job instead of quietly converging on a later pass. DEPLOYMENT.md documents the one-time production step: `supabase migration repair --status applied 20260806000005` before the next db push against a pre-existing project, since the baseline must not re-run where its 134 tables already exist. A new environment needs no repair — that is the point of the change. Verified from empty in a single pass with zero errors: 134 tables, all 8 verify:schema checks green including the lead pipeline smoke test, types.ts still in sync, validate-migrations green.

userStories.title: Pin search_path on SECURITY DEFINER functions
userStories.description: 50 SECURITY DEFINER functions do not pin search_path. A SECURITY DEFINER function without a pinned search_path can be tricked into resolving an unqualified name against an attacker-controlled schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Every SECURITY DEFINER function in the public schema declares SET search_path
The search_path check in scripts/verify-schema.mjs is promoted from a note to a blocking check
npm run verify:schema passes
The lead pipeline smoke test still passes, confirming no function broke
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06 in migration 20260806000003_pin_security_definer_search_path.sql. All 50 pinned via ALTER FUNCTION rather than rewriting bodies, so there is no chance of a transcription error in the logic and the migration is idempotent for the CI three-pass loop. Pin is `public, extensions, pg_temp`, not bare `public`: pgcrypto and uuid-ossp live in `extensions` both locally and on hosted Supabase, and generate_encryption_key() calls gen_random_bytes(), so a bare public pin would have broken it -- confirmed by calling it after the pin. pg_temp is named last precisely so it is searched last instead of first, which is the actual attack. The two functions already pinned (search_path=public and search_path=public, auth) were left alone. Demonstrated both ways on a clone of log_audit_event: unpinned, an authenticated attacker's `CREATE TEMP TABLE audit_logs` captured the audit row (temp=1, real=0) -- the audit trail silently diverted; pinned, the same attack captured nothing and the row reached the real table (temp=0, real=1). The search_path check in verify-schema.mjs is promoted from a note to blocking check 8, proven to fire by unpinning one function (exit 1) and restoring it (exit 0). Verified on a from-scratch three-pass rebuild: 146 tables, all 8 checks pass including the lead pipeline smoke test, validate-migrations passes on 88 files, and types.ts is still in sync.

userStories.title: Scope the twelve service-role RLS policies so anon cannot read or write them
userStories.description: Twelve policies are written as CREATE POLICY "Service role can manage X" ON t FOR ALL USING (true) with no TO clause. Postgres defaults that to TO PUBLIC, and Supabase grants ALL on every public table to anon, whose key ships in the frontend bundle. Every anonymous visitor therefore has unrestricted SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs, user_subscriptions, login_attempts, mfa_temp_codes, user_sessions, sso_login_sessions, gdpr_data_requests, account_deletion_scheduled, usage_tracking, rate_limit_entries, workflow_executions and workflow_execution_queue.
acceptanceCriteria: A corrective migration drops and recreates each of the twelve policies with TO service_role
No policy in the public schema grants ALL/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE to PUBLIC with a `true` qualifier on a non-public-data table
Connected as anon, SELECT and DELETE on audit_logs are denied; UPDATE on user_subscriptions is denied
The edge functions that write these tables still work (they use service_role, which is BYPASSRLS)
npm run verify:schema passes
The lead pipeline smoke test still passes
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06 in migration 20260806000001_scope_service_role_policies.sql. Scoped 16 policies to TO service_role - the 12 FOR ALL ones plus four FOR INSERT ones with the same defect (mfa_verification_logs, notifications, pii_encryption_audit, query_metrics); the notifications one let any visitor inject arbitrary title/message/data into any user's notification bell. Safe to narrow because every edge-function writer uses SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (the one exception, _shared/db-monitor.ts, has no callers) and every in-database writer (log_audit_event, notify_new_lead, record_login_attempt, check_rate_limit, update_usage_count, log_encryption_operation, start_workflow_execution) is SECURITY DEFINER. Narrowing user_subscriptions removed the admin health dashboard's cross-user read, so the migration adds an explicit "Admins can view all subscriptions" policy using the same has_role() pattern as audit_logs. Verified against a rebuilt Postgres with rows present: anon SELECT/DELETE returns 0 on audit_logs, user_subscriptions, user_sessions, login_attempts, mfa_temp_codes and notifications; owners still read their own rows; admin reads all 4 audit_logs; cross-tenant reads return 0; anon INSERT into notifications is denied by RLS. verify:schema passes including the lead pipeline smoke test, validate-migrations passes (86 files), and the migration is idempotent across the CI three-pass loop.

userStories.title: Stop anonymous visitors rewriting any user's public profile links
userStories.description: The "Anyone can increment link clicks" policy on links is FOR UPDATE USING (true) WITH CHECK (true). It is intended to let a visitor bump click_count, but it grants UPDATE on every column of every row - so any visitor can repoint any published profile link at a site of their choosing.
acceptanceCriteria: Connected as anon, UPDATE links SET url=... is denied
Click counting still works from a public profile page with no authenticated session
Either the policy is replaced by a SECURITY DEFINER increment_link_click(link_id) RPC, or WITH CHECK pins every column except click_count
If an RPC is added it pins search_path (see US-062) and is called by the profile click handler
npm run verify:schema passes
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06 in migration 20260806000002_fix_links_click_policy.sql. Took the RPC route: public.increment_link_clicks() already existed, was already SECURITY DEFINER and already pinned search_path, so the permissive UPDATE policy was redundant as well as dangerous - it was propping up nothing but the 'fallback: try direct update' branch in src/hooks/useProfileTracking.ts, which is removed alongside it. Migration drops the policy, grants EXECUTE on the function to anon/authenticated and adds a COMMENT warning against re-adding a permissive UPDATE policy. Verified: anon UPDATE of links.url is now UPDATE 0 and the url is intact, anon can still SELECT active links and still increments click_count through the RPC (0 -> 1), the owner can still update their own link, and another authenticated user gets UPDATE 0. Also fixed a double-count found while tracing the write path: FullProfilePage called trackLinkClick (which already increments) and then increment_link_clicks again, so every click counted twice. tsc unchanged at 356 errors, 274 tests pass, build passes, eslint clean on both changed files.

userStories.title: Make verify-schema.mjs fail on over-permissive RLS policies
userStories.description: The schema job checks that RLS is enabled on every table but never inspects what the policies grant, so both US-063 and US-064 passed CI. Add a blocking check for permissive policies that apply to PUBLIC with a `true` qualifier.
acceptanceCriteria: verify-schema.mjs gains a blocking check for policies with roles = {public} and qual/with_check `true` on write commands

Tables that are legitimately public (leads INSERT, analytics_views INSERT, mortgage_calculations INSERT, feature_catalog SELECT, the seo_* public reads) are allowlisted by name with a one-line reason each, as KNOWN_UNDEFINED_TABLES already does
The check fails on the current schema before US-063/US-064 land and passes after
npm run verify:schema passes with the new check enabled
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06 in scripts/verify-schema.mjs as check 3, 'no undeclared over-permissive RLS policy'. Flags any PERMISSIVE policy reaching anon/authenticated with an unconditional predicate (qual=true, or with_check=true for INSERT) unless declared. Two lists, following the KNOWN_UNDEFINED_TABLES precedent: PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN (13 entries, each with a one-line reason) for genuinely public reads and anonymous submissions, and KNOWN_OVERPERMISSIVE (12 entries) for pre-existing defects, each tagged with its story so the check can be blocking today. A companion loop emits a note when a KNOWN_OVERPERMISSIVE entry has been fixed, so the list cannot rot into hiding the next regression. Proven in both directions: re-introducing the exact US-063 shape (audit_logs FOR ALL USING (true)) and the US-064 shape (links FOR UPDATE USING (true)) makes it FAIL with exit code 1 naming both, dropping them returns exit code 0, and fixing an allowlisted entry emits the stale-entry note. Building it surfaced 12 pre-existing exposures now filed as US-067.

userStories.title: Move the PII encryption key off the client bundle
userStories.description: src/lib/pii.ts derives its AES-256-GCM master key from import.meta.env.VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Vite inlines every VITE_-prefixed value into the production bundle, so the key protecting encrypted_email and encrypted_phone is publicly downloadable. US-015/US-016 met their criteria, but the control protects nothing as deployed.
acceptanceCriteria: PII encrypt/decrypt happens where the key is not shipped to the browser - an edge function using PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY, or Supabase Vault
VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is removed from .env.example and from src/lib/pii.ts
src/hooks/useLeads.ts and src/hooks/useProfile.ts still round-trip PII correctly through the new path
src/lib/pii.test.ts still passes
A note records how existing enc:v1: values are re-keyed, or that the old key stays valid for decryption only
The plaintext email/phone columns retire on the schedule US-016 describes, once this lands
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06. Crypto moved into a new `pii-crypto` Edge Function holding PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY; src/lib/pii.ts is now a thin client that cannot decrypt anything on its own, which is the point. VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is gone from src/lib/pii.ts, .env.example and DEPLOYMENT.md's env table. Existing ciphertext survives: supabase/functions/_shared/encryption.ts already produced a byte-identical envelope to the old client (same enc:v1: prefix, PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100k iterations, 16-byte salt prepended to the 12-byte IV, base64-of-JSON), verified by reading both implementations side by side. So the migration is carrying the key across, not re-keying -- DEPLOYMENT.md §2.1 documents setting the function secret to the current VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY value, then removing it from Cloudflare Pages. Rotation is written up as a separate job needing a decrypt-old/re-encrypt-new backfill, and is the reason the plaintext columns should not retire until after it. Batched rather than per-value, or the leads list would have been two round trips per row: pii.ts gains encryptPIIBatch/decryptPIIBatch, useLeads decrypts a whole page in two calls and encrypts both fields in one, and values needing no work (empty, or lacking the enc:v1: prefix) short-circuit locally so an all-plaintext page makes no request at all. The function requires a JWT and is rate limited per user rather than per IP (agents behind one office NAT should not share a budget); confirmed check_rate_limit takes p_identifier text so a `user:<uuid>` key works. Encrypt fails closed, decrypt fails open. Found and removed an adjacent instance of the same defect while checking for leftovers: src/hooks/useEncryption.ts had zero callers and read VITE_ENCRYPTION_SECRET with a hardcoded fallback default -- another bundled key, one import away from being picked up. Deleted along with its env var. src/lib/encryption.ts is kept (pure primitives that take the secret as an argument and read no env var, plus its tests guard the envelope the edge function must stay compatible with) with a header note saying so. pii.test.ts rewritten against a stubbed edge function, covering position preservation, the local short-circuits, and both failure directions: 14 tests, suite total 274 -> 277. tsc unchanged at 321, eslint 0 errors, build and verify:schema green.

userStories.title: Fix the free-tool tables: prospect list exposure, visitor IP leak, and broken anonymous email capture
userStories.description: The /tools/* lead-gen tables carry `ALL TO authenticated USING (true)`, so any registered user can read and delete every prospect email, name, phone number and brokerage the free tools have ever captured. instagram_bio_analyses and listing_descriptions additionally carry `SELECT TO anon USING (true)` over rows holding visitor ip_address and user_agent. And the tools' own anonymous email capture is broken: the client issues .insert().select().single(), whose RETURNING needs a SELECT policy that anon does not have, so the insert is rejected and the code rethrows.
acceptanceCriteria: Reading the lead-gen tables is restricted to admins (has_role) and service_role; anonymous submission still works
No anonymous SELECT over rows carrying ip_address or user_agent
Anonymous email capture works end to end on both /tools/instagram-bio-analyzer and /tools/listing-description-generator — verified as anon, not reasoned about
content_suggestions is scoped to its owner (suggested_by) or to admins rather than every authenticated user
seo_alert_rules is not readable by anon
Every entry this story covers is removed from KNOWN_OVERPERMISSIVE in scripts/verify-schema.mjs
npm run verify:schema passes with the shrunken list and emits no stale-entry notes
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06 in migration 20260806000004_scope_free_tool_tables.sql plus the two tool pages. Access model applied uniformly to the eight lead-gen tables: anon INSERT only, authenticated nothing, admin SELECT via has_role, service_role ALL. Dropped the eight `ALL TO authenticated USING (true)` policies and the two `SELECT TO anon` policies over rows carrying ip_address/user_agent. content_suggestions is now suggested_by = auth.uid() OR admin; seo_alert_rules is admin-only. The broken anonymous capture is fixed on the client rather than by widening the policy: both tools now generate the row id with crypto.randomUUID() and insert it, dropping the .select().single() whose implied RETURNING needed a SELECT policy anon must not have. Exercising it as anon caught a regression that reading the diff would not have: initialize_bio_email_sequence and init_listing_email_sequence are AFTER INSERT triggers on the capture tables that write seven placeholder rows into the *_email_sequences tables, and both were SECURITY INVOKER -- so with the blanket policy gone they ran as anon and their inserts were refused, aborting the visitor's capture. The bio one has a WHEN (new.email_sequence_started = true) clause that only the real client path satisfies, so a careless test would have missed it. Both are now SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned per US-062 -- correct because those rows are system-generated and should not be forgeable by a visitor. Also fixed an adjacent bug that was unreachable while capture was broken: the Instagram tool passed `captureData?.id || analysisId` as the edge function's analysisId, but send-bio-analyzer-email looks that id up in instagram_bio_email_captures and stores it as email_capture_id, so it wants the capture row -- the fallback would have failed the lookup. Now passes the capture id. Verified as anon: both captures succeed, 7 and 6 sequence rows are created, and anon reads back 0 from every affected table; a freshly registered user reads and deletes 0; admin still reads the funnel. KNOWN_OVERPERMISSIVE is now empty alongside KNOWN_UNDEFINED_TABLES. Fresh three-pass rebuild green on all 8 checks, validate-migrations green on 89 files, tsc 322 -> 321, 274 tests, build and lint clean.

userStories.title: Restore the signup trigger so a new account gets a profile, a role and a subscription
userStories.description: public.handle_new_user() exists but nothing attaches it to auth.users. The squashed baseline (20260806000005) came from a public-schema dump, and a trigger on auth.users is not part of the public schema, so US-060 dropped it. Inserting into auth.users on a database built from supabase/migrations/ creates 0 profiles and 0 user_roles. Signup therefore produces no profile (useAuthStore.signUp burns ~3.1s retrying), no role (getSecurityContext defaults everyone to 'user', so nobody can ever be an admin), and no subscription (create_default_subscription fires on profiles INSERT, so it never runs and useSubscriptionLimits' .single() throws). The current function body also regressed: it sets username to the first 9 hex chars of the UUID, discarding the username the user chose and Register.tsx validated.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration creates the on_auth_user_created AFTER INSERT trigger on auth.users executing public.handle_new_user()
handle_new_user uses COALESCE(new.raw_user_meta_data->>'username', split_part(new.email,'@',1)) rather than a UUID prefix, with a collision fallback so a taken username cannot abort the signup

On a freshly rebuilt database, INSERT INTO auth.users produces exactly one profiles row, one user_roles row with role 'user', and one subscriptions row on the free plan — verified by executing it, not by reading the migration
A signup whose chosen username is already taken still succeeds, with a deterministic suffixed username
npm run verify:schema passes
npm run test:run and npm run build still pass
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-08 in migration 20260808000001_restore_signup_trigger.sql. Recreated on_auth_user_created (AFTER INSERT ON auth.users) and rewrote handle_new_user to use the requested username. Username derivation was extracted into public.derive_available_username(requested, email, user_id) so it is testable on its own: it lowercases, strips anything usernameSchema would reject, clamps to 30 chars, falls back to user-<8 hex of uuid> when the result is under 3 chars or hits the RESERVED_USERNAMES list from src/lib/usernameValidation.ts, then suffixes -2, -3 ... on collision (bounded at 50, then falls back to the uuid). Normalising to lower case matters beyond tidiness: profiles_username_key is a case-SENSITIVE unique index while check_username_available() compares with LOWER(), so mixed-case signups could otherwise create two profiles the availability check treats as one. Making profiles_username_key itself case-insensitive is deliberately left out — it can fail on existing production data; raised as a follow-up rather than forced here. Errors are NOT swallowed: a signup that cannot provision must fail loudly rather than recreate the state this story exists to fix. Verified against a rebuilt Postgres by executing seven signups, not by reading the migration: chosen username janesmith -> janesmith with role user and a free/active subscription at max_listings 3; a second janesmith -> janesmith-2; JaneSmith -> janesmith-3 (case-insensitive collision); no metadata -> bobjones from the email local part; admin -> user-55555555 (reserved); !! -> user-66666666 (junk); a 44-char name -> clamped to 30. 7 profiles, 7 roles, 7 subscriptions from 7 auth.users inserts. Re-applying the migration leaves exactly one trigger on auth.users. verify:schema green on all 8 checks, validate-migrations green on 3 files.

userStories.title: Fix public lead capture: the three inquiry forms write columns that do not exist
userStories.description: src/lib/leadSubmission.ts inserts into leads using agent_id, type, data and referrer. The real columns are user_id (NOT NULL), lead_type (NOT NULL), form_data and referrer_url. BuyerInquiryForm, SellerInquiryForm and HomeValuationForm all use it, and all three are reachable from the public profile via LeadFormModal (FullProfilePage.tsx:617, LeadCaptureCTA.tsx:151). Every submission is rejected by PostgREST, retried three times, and shown to the visitor as a generic failure. tsc already reports this as src/lib/leadSubmission.ts(41,21): error TS2769.
acceptanceCriteria: The three inquiry forms submit through the submit-lead edge function, which already does rate limiting, validation and sanitisation — not through a repaired direct insert
A lead submitted from each of the three forms lands in the leads table with the correct user_id and lead_type
The TS2769 at leadSubmission.ts:41 is gone and the tsc count drops by at least one
src/lib/leadSubmission.ts is either deleted or reduced to a thin wrapper over the edge function with no invented columns
npm run test:run and npm run build still pass
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-08. src/lib/leadSubmission.ts now calls the submit-lead edge function instead of inserting directly, which is what ContactBlock.tsx already did — renaming the four columns in place was rejected because a direct browser insert also bypasses submit-lead's rate limiting, validation and sanitisation, and the leads policy "Anyone can submit leads" is WITH CHECK (true) so it would accept anything. The three forms send a nested "data" bag, so submitLead() now splits it: keys with a real column (priceRange, timeline, address, preApproved, message) are lifted to price_range/timeline/property_address/preapproved/message, and the remainder (propertyType, bedrooms, bathrooms, squareFeet, yearBuilt, condition, reason) goes to leads.form_data. That required two additions to submit-lead, which previously dropped both: a form_data passthrough with a sanitiser (keys and values sanitised and length-capped, nested objects dropped rather than walked, 40-key cap) and "source", which the function accepted in its payload but never copied into the insert. The three-retry loop is gone — the edge function is rate limited at 5/min per IP, so retrying a rejection just burned the visitor's budget, and the old loop retried validation failures it could never recover from. Verified by replaying the exact payload each of the three forms produces through the same mapping and inserting the resulting column set: buyer -> price_range 400k-500k plus form_data{bedrooms,propertyType}; seller -> property_address "12 Elm St" plus form_data{reason,bedrooms,bathrooms,propertyType}; valuation -> property_address "9 Oak Ave" plus form_data{bedrooms,bathrooms,condition,yearBuilt,squareFeet,propertyType}. tsc 148 -> 147 (the TS2769 at leadSubmission.ts:41 is gone), 277 tests, build clean.

userStories.title: profiles.email does not exist, and five edge functions select it — every lead notification is silently dead
userStories.description: The column is email_display; the agent's real address lives in auth.users.email. Five functions select profiles.email, all written best-effort with no error branch, so the query 400s, profile?.email is undefined and the path silently no-ops: submit-lead:99 (the agent notification email AND the Zapier webhook, since zapier_webhook_url comes from the same failed query), notify-lead:71 (the trigger-driven new-lead notification, which then returns HTTP 200 with reason 'no_agent_email' and a comment reading 'Nothing to notify; not an error'), submit-contact:66 (contact-form alerts), and stripe-webhook:405 (the dunning email on invoice.payment_failed, so customers whose card fails are never told).
acceptanceCriteria: All five call sites resolve the agent's address from auth.users (via auth.admin.getUserById or a SECURITY DEFINER helper), not from a non-existent profiles column
A lead submitted through submit-lead produces an agent notification email and fires the configured Zapier webhook — verified by executing the function, not by reading it
notify-lead returns a failure rather than HTTP 200 when it cannot resolve a recipient, and logs it
invoice.payment_failed sends the dunning email
No .select() anywhere in supabase/functions/ names a column that does not exist on the target table (see US-089)
npm run verify:schema passes
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-08. Added supabase/functions/_shared/agent-contact.ts with getAgentContact(supabase, userId), which reads the real profile columns (full_name, email_display, phone, zapier_webhook_url, notification_preferences) and resolves the account address from auth.users via auth.admin.getUserById — profiles has never had an "email" column. All four call sites now use it: submit-lead (the agent notification AND the Zapier webhook, which came from the same failed query and so had never fired for anyone), notify-lead, submit-contact, and stripe-webhook's dunning email. Each site previously destructured the result with no error branch, so PostgREST rejecting the whole query for the unknown column surfaced as undefined and the path silently skipped; they now log an explicit error when the address cannot be resolved. notify-lead changed behaviour deliberately: it used to return HTTP 200 with reason "no_agent_email", which every single lead hit, so a total failure looked like a considered no-op — it now returns an AGENT_EMAIL_UNRESOLVED error. Verified by executing the exact queries getAgentContact issues against a rebuilt Postgres (they return rows; the old one raises: column "email" does not exist) and by re-running the column sweep across all 87 edge functions: 6 bad column selects -> 0. The systemic guard that stops this class returning is US-082.

userStories.title: Twelve views bypass RLS for anon, leaking Stripe IDs and cross-tenant lead activity
userStories.description: All twelve views in the public schema are owned by postgres and none sets security_invoker, so under Postgres semantics they read their base tables with the owner's privileges and RLS on those tables does not apply. All twelve grant SELECT to anon, whose key ships in the frontend bundle. Verified as anon: subscriptions returns 0 rows but user_subscription_details returns the row including stripe_customer_id and stripe_subscription_id; lead_activities returns 0 rows but lead_activity_summary returns per-lead call/email/meeting counts across all tenants. The other ten leak aggregate funnel and SEO metrics.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration sets security_invoker = on for all twelve views in the public schema
SELECT is revoked from anon on every view with no public purpose
As anon, user_subscription_details and lead_activity_summary return 0 rows; as the owning user they still return that user's own rows
The admin dashboards and free-tool funnels that legitimately read these views still work
verify:schema fails on any anon-granted view lacking security_invoker (see US-089)
npm run verify:schema passes
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-08 in migration 20260808000002_close_anon_data_exposure.sql. security_invoker = on for all twelve views, plus REVOKE SELECT from anon and authenticated on eleven of them. Only lead_activity_summary has a caller in the application (src/hooks/useLeadActivities.ts, twice, for the signed-in agent's own leads); the other eleven are referenced by nothing but the generated types, so a grant nothing uses is a grant waiting to be misused. Verified as anon on a rebuilt Postgres with rows present: user_subscription_details and lead_activity_summary both now return "permission denied for view" where before they returned the Stripe customer/subscription ids and cross-tenant call/email counts. Verified as the owning agent that lead_activity_summary still returns their 1 row, and as a second tenant that it returns 0 — the half of the check that catches over-tightening. That owner-side verification was impossible before this session: scripts/supabase-prelude.sql never granted USAGE ON SCHEMA auth, so auth.uid() raised "permission denied for schema auth" for anon/authenticated and every owner-scoped policy errored rather than evaluating. The grant is now in the prelude. Note for future tests: the prelude's auth.uid() shim reads request.jwt.claim.sub, not the request.jwt.claims JSON that production reads, so set both.

userStories.title: enterprise_sso_config exposes its OIDC client secret and SAML certificate to anonymous visitors
userStories.description: CREATE POLICY "Users can view active SSO configs for their domain" ON public.enterprise_sso_config FOR SELECT USING (active = true) has no TO clause, so Postgres defaults it to TO PUBLIC — anon included. The table holds oidc_client_secret, saml_certificate, oidc_client_id and every endpoint URL. Verified as anon: the full row comes back including the client secret. verify:schema's over-permissive-policy check misses it because the qualifier is `active = true` rather than a literal `true`.

userStories.title: Public review submission is impossible, and the obvious fix would publish unmoderated text
userStories.description: /…/review (SubmitReview.tsx:76, routed at App.tsx:220) is a public unauthenticated page that inserts into testimonials with user_id set to the agent's id. The only INSERT policy is WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id), so as anon the insert is rejected — verified: 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "testimonials"'. Every review submission fails with "Submission failed". leads has an explicit "Anyone can submit leads" policy; testimonials has no equivalent. The trap: testimonials.is_published DEFAULTS TO TRUE, so adding an anon INSERT policy on its own would let anyone publish arbitrary text straight onto any agent's public profile with no moderation.

npm run verify:schema passes

The policy and the default had to move together, exactly as this story warned: testimonials.is_published DEFAULTED TO TRUE, so an anon INSERT policy on its own would have let anyone publish arbitrary text straight onto any agent's public profile. The default is now false, and the new policy FORCES is_published = false in its WITH CHECK rather than trusting the default, so a caller cannot pass true explicitly. It also requires the target profile to be published (a review cannot be used to probe for or attach rows to non-public accounts) and bounds rating 1-5, client_name 1-100 and review 1-2000 as a backstop for the direct insert RLS permits.
