The "pre-existing harness failure" recorded above was not the app: src/integrations/supabase/client.ts throws at import when VITE_SUPABASE_URL/VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are unset, playwright-e2e.config.ts passed no env, and neither does the CI job — so the SPA never mounted and every spec ran against a blank <body>. The config now supplies placeholders on the dev server's own origin (index.html's CSP connect-src is 'self' plus the agentbio.net hosts, so any other localhost port is refused before Playwright's router sees it). npm run test:e2e is 15/15 green.

All three specs in tests/e2e/public-profile-visibility.spec.ts now run and pass: a pending listing appears on the public page, turning off "show sold properties" hides them from a logged-out visitor, and they are shown again when the toggle is on. They run logged out, which was always the point.

userStories.title: Remove the hard-coded trust claims: "Available Now", "Verified Agent", "Responds in < 1 hour", "Trusted by Hundreds", SOC 2, and the fabricated stats block
userStories.description: ProfileHeader.tsx:82-85 shows 'Available Now' with a pulsing green dot for every agent, always; 89-92 shows 'Verified Agent' though no verification exists. FullProfilePage.tsx:416 sets responseTime: '< 1 hour' and StickyActionBar.tsx:225 repeats it with no data behind it. SocialProofBanner.tsx:69 says 'Trusted by Hundreds of Happy Clients' with 1 sale and 0 reviews. pageBuilder.ts:411-415 defaults the Stats block to '150 Homes Sold', '98% Client Satisfaction', '15 Years', '$50M in Sales' and StatsBlock.tsx:60 publishes it unchanged; the Bio block defaults to 'Your Name' / '[Your City]'. Register.tsx:243 claims 'SOC 2 compliant'; Register.tsx:272 says '2,500+ agents' while Landing.tsx:210,525 says '5,000+'; the Landing JSON-LD carries ratingValue 4.8 and Login.tsx:243-252 quotes a named testimonial. These are advertising claims on a licensed professional's page and on the company's own signup.
acceptanceCriteria: The static availability, verification, response-time and 'hundreds' strings are removed; a response-time badge appears only when computed from leads.first_responded_at - created_at over the last 90 days
'Verified' is replaced by 'Licensed' and shown only when license_number and license_state are present
Stats block defaults to an empty list (the block already renders 'Add stats in the settings panel' when empty) and Bio block defaults come from the profile
SOC 2 wording is removed unless an attestation exists; agent counts and the aggregate rating come from one config value or are removed; the login testimonial is real or removed
userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-09-02. The response-time aggregate was verified by execution against a real Postgres.

ON THE AGENT'S PUBLIC PAGE:
- "Available Now", with a pulsing green dot, was rendered for EVERY agent unconditionally. Removed rather than made conditional — nothing in this product tracks availability, so there is no signal to condition it on.
- "Verified Agent" was shown to every visitor although no verification process exists anywhere in the product. Replaced with "Licensed in {state}", shown only when license_number AND license_state are present. That states a fact the agent asserted rather than an endorsement the platform never made.
- "Responds in < 1 hour" appeared twice: as a hard-coded responseTime string on the profile header and as literal text in StickyActionBar. The sticky-bar line is gone; the header badge is now computed or absent.
- "Trusted by Hundreds of Happy Clients" was rendered above 1 sale and 0 reviews. The heading is "Track Record" and the numbers speak for themselves.

THE RESPONSE TIME IS NOW REAL. Migration 20260902000010 adds public_agent_response_hours(uuid): the MEDIAN hours from leads.first_responded_at - created_at over 90 days.

Three deliberate choices. It is SECURITY DEFINER returning a single number, because `leads` is readable only by its owner and assignee (US-097, US-105) and must stay that way — a visitor must never be able to enumerate an agent's leads. It is the median, not the mean, because one week-late reply would wreck an average and "typically responds in" is what the badge means. And it returns NULL below FIVE responded leads in the window, because a median over one or two responses is not a track record — no badge beats an invented one, which is this story's whole point.

Verified by execution: 4 responded leads -> NULL; a 5th -> median 2.0h; adding a 200-hour outlier -> still 2.0h (a mean would have jumped to ~35h); ageing every lead past 90 days -> NULL; and as anon, the function returns a value while SELECT on leads still returns 0 rows.

IN THE PAGE BUILDER:
- The Stats block defaulted to '150 Homes Sold', '98% Client Satisfaction', '15 Years', '$50M in Sales' and StatsBlock published them unchanged — dropping the block onto a page put four invented figures on a licensed agent's profile under their name. Now an empty list; StatsBlock already renders "Add stats in the settings panel".
- The Bio block defaulted to 'Your Name' and '[Your City] … [X] years of experience' — bracketed placeholders that publish verbatim. Now blank, with autoPopulateBioBlock filling title, subtitle and description from the profile (subtitle now included; it was pinned to the default).

ON THE COMPANY'S OWN PAGES:
- The landing page's JSON-LD carried aggregateRating 4.8 over 523 reviews. This is the most serious of the set: Google renders stars in search results from that field, so it is a fabricated claim published to everyone who searches, and a structured-data policy violation besides. Removed.
- "2,500+ agents" on signup and "5,000+" on the landing page — two invented numbers for the same thing, one click apart. Both now come from src/config/marketing-claims.ts, which deliberately carries no number: the line reads "Join agents growing their business with AgentBio" until there is a query behind a count.
- "SOC 2 compliant" is replaced by three things the code actually does — RLS on every table, lead contact details encrypted at rest, TLS in transit. No attestation exists in or referenced from this repo.
- The login page quoted a named testimonial from "Sarah Mitchell, Top Producer, Miami". Removed. A fabricated endorsement attributed to a named person is a different thing from optimistic copy, and this product sells to licensed professionals who are themselves regulated on exactly that point.

TESTS: responseTime.test.ts (7), the important one being that null and nonsensical values render NOTHING rather than a fallback claim.

VERIFICATION: npx tsc --noEmit 0 errors; npm run test:run 446 passed, 44 files (was 439); verify:schema 18/18; validate-migrations OK (23 files); gen-supabase-types --check up to date; eslint 0 errors. Grepped the tree for every removed phrase — the only remaining hits are the comments explaining why they went.

userStories.title: Public listing UX: the modal shows a placeholder for photos the card displays, stray "0"s, a leaking scroll listener, and dead buttons
userStories.description: usePublicProfile.ts:188 normalises photos with toStringList, which returns [] for null; ListingDetailModal.tsx:73-76 does `listing.photos || (listing.image ? [listing.image] : null)`, and [] is truthy, so a legacy single-image listing shows the grey placeholder in the modal while ListingCard.tsx:46 shows the photo. ProfileHeader.tsx:124,131,138 and FeaturedListingsCarousel.tsx:277-293 use `stats.propertiesSold && ...`, so a new agent's badge row renders '00'. QuickNav.tsx:20-24 calls window.addEventListener in the render body with no cleanup; each state change adds a listener and each scroll fires all of them. SoldProperties.tsx:78-83 renders 'View All {n} Sold Properties' with no handler, duplicates the stats bar above it and formats missing prices as '$0K+'. StickyActionBar's desktop panel overlaps content between 768 and 1150px and its mobile panel overlaps QuickNav's scroll-to-top. FullProfilePage.tsx:165-167 renders NotFound for any error, including a transient network failure; 57-66 uses .single() for the custom-page check and silently skips the redirect on PGRST116. Forms call setValue without shouldValidate, two error boxes lack role=alert, and two DialogContents have no DialogTitle.
acceptanceCriteria: The modal shows the same photo the card shows for every listing in the seeded fixtures
No literal 0 is rendered by a falsy guard; the badge rows use > 0 or Boolean()
QuickNav registers one passive scroll listener in an effect with cleanup
'View All' expands the sold list; the duplicate stats bar is removed; the floating panels do not overlap content or each other at 375, 768, 1024 and 1280px widths
A load error shows a retry state and only a real 404 shows NotFound; the custom-page check uses maybeSingle with limit(1)
Form selects validate on change, all error boxes carry role=alert, and every DialogContent has a DialogTitle (visually hidden where needed)
userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-09-02. Every item covered; the two with real logic behind them are held to regression tests. (1) THE MODAL PLACEHOLDER. usePublicProfile normalises photos with toStringList, which returns [] for null — and [] is TRUTHY, so `listing.photos || (listing.image ? [listing.image] : null)` never reached the fallback. A legacy single-image listing showed the grey placeholder in the modal while ListingCard, which checks `listing.image || listing.photos?.[0]`, showed the photo. Same listing, two answers. Now `photos?.length ? photos : image ? [image] : null`. (2) THE STRAY ZEROS. `stats?.propertiesSold && …` short-circuits to 0 when the count is 0, and React renders 0. Two side by side gave a new agent's badge row "00". Confirmed by probe: the row rendered
0
. Fixed in ProfileHeader (sold, rating, years) and FeaturedListingsCarousel (beds, baths, sqft) by leading with the comparison so the expression is boolean. (3) THE LISTENER LEAK. QuickNav called window.addEventListener in the RENDER BODY with no cleanup. Every render added a listener; every scroll fired all of them; each called setState, which rendered again and added another. Unbounded growth for as long as a visitor scrolled the public page. Now one passive listener in an effect with cleanup, plus an initial call so the button reflects the position the page loaded at. (4) SOLD PROPERTIES. "View All {n} Sold Properties" had no onClick — a button naming a number that did nothing. It expands now and toggles back. The volume figures counted every sold listing including unpriced ones, so an agent with no prices recorded saw "$0K+" and an average dragged toward zero; only priced sales contribute, and the volume tiles are hidden when there is no volume. The summary bar is opt-in (showStats, default false) because SocialProofBanner already shows properties-sold and volume a few sections above on the same page. (5) THE FLOATING PANELS. The desktop side panel was `hidden md:block` — a 200px panel pinned to right-6 from 768px, where the content column still runs full width, so it sat on top of the content until about 1150px. It is `hidden xl:block` now and the mobile bar is `xl:hidden`, so exactly one of the two is present at every width; they previously left no gap only by overlapping. QuickNav's scroll-to-top moved from bottom-20 to bottom-36, because StickyActionBar's expanded mobile panel is `fixed bottom-20 left-0 right-0` and covered the full width at exactly that height. (6) ERROR HANDLING. `if (error || !data) return ` told a visitor who hit a transient network failure that the agent does not exist — on a page an agent hands out on a business card — with no way to retry but guessing at a reload. Only PGRST116 (or "Profile not found") is a 404 now; anything else renders ProfileLoadError with a retry that refetches. The custom-page check used .single(), which errors on none AND on several, and the catch treated both as "no custom page" — so an agent with two active published pages silently kept the default profile. Now maybeSingle with limit(1) and a deterministic order. (7) FORMS AND DIALOGS. Every Select's setValue passes { shouldValidate: true }, so a required select clears its error when answered rather than at submit. role="alert" added to the six error boxes that lacked it. The two DialogContents without a DialogTitle (LeadFormModal, the home-valuation dialog) have visually hidden ones — Radix requires a title, and without one a screen reader announces the dialog unnamed. TESTS: SoldProperties.test.tsx (7) covers the expand toggle, the summary bar being off by default, and that "$0K+" never renders. ProfileHeader.test.tsx (4) covers the empty badge row, the licence badge from US-111, and that availability is never claimed. Both verified against the original defects: restoring the falsy guard makes the badge-row assertion fail (asserting on the row's own textContent, not the page's — a looser check passed against the bug and was tightened). VERIFICATION: npx tsc --noEmit 0 errors; npm run test:run 457 passed, 46 files (was 446); verify:schema 18/18; eslint 0 errors. NOT VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: the responsive claim. The breakpoint pairing (xl:hidden / hidden xl:block) and the bottom-36 clearance are reasoned from the CSS and are correct by construction, but I did not render at 375/768/1024/1280 to look. The e2e harness that would do it is the one documented as broken in US-108. CAUGHT BY THE PRE-COMMIT HOOK, worth recording: my first version of the SoldProperties change put `useState` AFTER the component's early return, a react-hooks/rules-of-hooks error. eslint --fix in the husky hook rejected the commit. I had run `npx eslint src/` myself and read the trailing "0 errors and 1 warning potentially fixable with the --fix option" line as the result — that line counts only what --fix can repair, not the total. The line that matters is "✖ N problems (E errors, W warnings)". Hook moved above the return; eslint now reports 0 errors across src/ by that measure.

userStories.title: Public page accessibility and the review page
userStories.description: ListingCard.tsx:152 hides save/share behind opacity-0 group-hover, invisible on touch devices, and nests two <button>s inside a role=button card whose onKeyDown handles Enter but not Space. ListingDetailModal.tsx:195-218 is a hand-rolled overlay with no role=dialog, aria-modal, focus trap or focus restore, and its icon buttons (233-257, 282-295) have no aria-label; the page already uses the Radix Dialog elsewhere. FeaturedListingsCarousel.tsx:91-99 auto-rotates every 4 s, pauses on hover only, and ignores prefers-reduced-motion. SubmitReview.tsx:241-252 requires a client email 'for verification only', never stores it (no column) and never verifies; 147-148 promises '{agent} will be notified' and no notification exists (the only testimonials trigger is track_testimonials_usage); transaction_type 'both' renders as Seller in TestimonialCard.tsx:104; the star buttons have no accessible name; and the public profile has no 'Leave a review' link, only RequestTestimonialModal builds the URL.
acceptanceCriteria: Card actions are visible below md, the card is a single interactive element or uses a link plus separate buttons, and Space activates it
ListingDetailModal uses @/components/ui/dialog with labelled controls; the carousel pauses on touch and does not auto-rotate under prefers-reduced-motion
npm run test:a11y passes on the public profile with a listing modal open
SubmitReview either drops the email field or stores it and sends an agent notification through an edge function; 'both' renders as 'Buyer & Seller'; stars have aria-labels
A 'Worked with {name}? Leave a review' link appears near the testimonials section
userStories.notes:
Done and verified by execution.

CARD / MODAL / CAROUSEL
- ListingCard: the role="button" container with two real <button>s nested inside it is gone. The card's control is now the address, a real <button> (so Space works — the old onKeyDown checked Enter only), with an sr-only "View listing: " prefix so the accessible name says which listing. The div keeps its click for pointer users but no longer claims to be a control. Save/share moved from `opacity-0 group-hover:` to `md:opacity-0 md:group-hover: md:focus-within:` — visible below md, where there is no hover at all.
- ListingDetailModal: now @/components/ui/dialog (Radix), so role=dialog, aria-modal, focus trap, focus restore and Escape come from the primitive instead of being absent. The hand-rolled backdrop, the manual document.body.style.overflow and the manual Escape handler are removed. Save/share/close have aria-labels.
- FeaturedListingsCarousel: honours prefers-reduced-motion, and pauses on touchstart and focus, not hover only.

REVIEW PAGE
- The email field is dropped, not stored. `testimonials` has no client_email column (checked against src/integrations/supabase/types.ts), nothing verified anything, and adding a plaintext PII column while leads are moving the other way (US-086 encryption) would have been a step backwards — plus gdpr-export/deletion would have had to learn about it. The "for verification only" copy is gone with it.
- The success screen's "{agent} will be notified" was false; it is true now. Submission goes through a new submit-review edge function (the submit-lead shape: rate limited via check_rate_limit, validated by a new validateReviewData, service-role insert with is_published forced to false, then a real agent email through _shared/email.ts createTestimonialNotificationEmail + an audit-log row). The anon INSERT policy from 20260808000004 stays as the backstop for the direct path. The copy now says the agent reviews each one before it appears, which is what the moderation default actually does.
- SubmitReview also now treats a 4xx as a failure: functions.invoke() rejects only on transport errors, so a rate-limit or validation response arrived as data.success === false and would have rendered the thank-you screen.
- transaction_type 'both' renders as "Buyer & Seller" via a new src/lib/testimonialLabels.ts; an unrecognised value now renders no badge rather than being guessed at as "Seller".
- Star buttons have aria-label ("1 star" … "5 stars") and aria-pressed.
- ReviewInvite ("Worked with {name}? Leave a review") sits under the testimonials section on FullProfilePage, as a real <Link>. The section is no longer gated on testimonials.length: the invitation matters most on a profile with no reviews yet, and TestimonialSection already returns null when the list is empty.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS — the a11y suite was testing nothing.
src/integrations/supabase/client.ts throws at import when VITE_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY are unset. playwright-a11y.config.ts passed no env and neither does the CI job, so the SPA never mounted, every page under test was a blank <body>, and axe reported zero violations on all five. I confirmed this directly: the page body was empty and not one /rest/v1 request was made. The config now passes placeholder VITE_* values pointing at the dev server's own origin — it has to be that origin, because index.html ships a CSP whose connect-src is 'self' plus the agentbio.net hosts, and the browser refused a 127.0.0.1:54321 connection before Playwright's router saw it. assertAppRendered() is now a tripwire so a blank page fails instead of passing. With the app actually rendering, all five existing baselines still hold exactly (landing 3, the rest 1), so the numbers were measured against a working app originally.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- tsc --noEmit: 0 errors. vitest: 52 files, 482 tests, all passing (was 49/474).
- eslint on every touched file: 0 errors (15 warnings, all pre-existing react/no-unescaped-entities and one pre-existing `any` on SubmitReview's profile state).
- verify-schema against the local Postgres: all 18 checks pass.
- npm run test:a11y: 6/6 pass, including the new 'public profile with a listing modal open' case, which opens the modal by clicking the card's address button and asserts getByRole('dialog') is visible.
- Every guard was proved to go red on the original defect: reverting the badge ternary fails the 'both' test; removing the data.success check fails the SubmitReview failure test; reverting ListingCard fails all three of its tests; removing the reduced-motion/touch/focus handling fails three carousel tests; and reverting ListingCard+ListingDetailModal fails the new a11y modal case (the address button does not exist to click).

NOT VERIFIED
- submit-review has never run: there is no Deno runtime or live Supabase here. Its validation and email template are covered by vitest (they read Deno.env inside the function, not at module scope), and log_audit_event's argument names are checked by verify-schema, but the request path itself is untested end to end.
- No email was actually sent; RESEND_API_KEY is not set here.

ALSO: removed lead_report_2026-09-01.pdf and performance_2026-09-01.pdf, which the test suite writes into the repo root and which I committed by accident in 887a038 (US-085). The older *_2026-08-08.pdf files predate this work and are left for US-121.

userStories.title: Sharing a listing shares the profile, and every social unfurl shows the generic AgentBio card instead of the agent
userStories.description: ListingCard.tsx:82,89, ListingDetailModal.tsx:150 and FeaturedListingsCarousel.tsx:131 share window.location.href; there is no ?listing= deep link and no state restore, so the recipient lands at the top of the profile. The JSON-LD injected inside the modal (ListingDetailModal.tsx:196-201) can never be indexed because the modal has no URL. public/_redirects is '/* /index.html 200' with no Pages Function or prerender, so iMessage, Facebook and Slack unfurls of agentbio.net/jane show index.html's generic tags ('Real Estate Agent Bio Page Builder', Cover.png) rather than the agent's name and headshot that SEOHead sets client-side. Agents share their link from business cards and Instagram; the unfurl is the first impression.
acceptanceCriteria: /:username?listing=<id> opens that listing's modal on load and is the URL every share button copies
A Cloudflare Pages Function for /:username (and the listing variant) injects the agent's title, description, og:image and JSON-LD server-side for crawlers, verified with curl -A facebookexternalhit
Sharing a listing from a phone produces an unfurl with the property photo and address
userStories.notes:
Done. All three criteria met and verified by execution.

(1) DEEP LINK. The detail modal was component state, so it had no URL at all. It is now derived from ?listing=<id> (src/lib/listingShare.ts + FullProfilePage), which gives it an address, makes Back close it, and makes a pasted link open the right property. A query parameter rather than a path segment because /:username/:listingId would collide with /:username/review, and the profile route is already /:slug at the bottom of the table. An id that matches nothing renders the profile, not an error. All three share buttons — card, modal, carousel — now build the listing URL instead of window.location.href, dropping any query and hash the visitor arrived with so a tracking parameter is not passed on to whoever they send it to.

(2) PAGES FUNCTION. functions/[username].ts, with the pure half in functions/_lib/social-meta.ts. A crawler gets index.html with its head replaced — the agent's name, bio, avatar and RealEstateAgent JSON-LD, or the property's address, price, photo and SingleFamilyResidence JSON-LD when ?listing= is present. A person gets next(), byte for byte, with no database call at all. Everything that can fail — no binding, unreachable database, unknown username, 4s timeout — falls through to next(); a social card is not worth risking the page for. The old tags are stripped rather than duplicated, values are attribute-escaped, and </script> inside the JSON-LD is escaped. The route file is the only thing in functions/ that is routable: both test files live under underscore-prefixed directories, because Cloudflare Pages would otherwise publish /username-route.test.

(3) VERIFIED WITH curl -A facebookexternalhit. wrangler needs a Cloudflare login this sandbox does not have, and a Pages Function is just an async (context) => Response, so scripts/preview-social-meta.mjs serves it over node:http with a stub PostgREST and the real index.html. Actual output:
  /jane            → <title>Jane Doe — Associate Broker at Summit Realty</title>, og:image the avatar, og:type profile, canonical, RealEstateAgent JSON-LD with worksFor and areaServed.
  /jane?listing=…  → <title>412 Maple Avenue, Salt Lake City, UT — $525,000</title>, og:image the property photo, og:description "$525,000 · 3 bd · 2 ba · 1,980 sqft. Listed by Jane Doe.", og:type website, SingleFamilyResidence JSON-LD with PostalAddress, floorSize and an Offer.
  Chrome UA        → index.html unchanged, Cover.png and all.
  x-agentbio-prerender is set on /jane and absent on /dashboard.

TESTS: 25 new unit tests (functions/_lib/social-meta.test.ts, functions/_tests/username-route.test.ts — vitest now includes functions/**/*.test.ts, and tsconfig includes functions/, which was type-checked by nothing before) and 4 e2e specs (tests/e2e/listing-deep-link.spec.ts): the parameter opens the right property, an unknown id renders the profile, opening pushes the URL and Back closes it, and the share button copies the listing URL rather than the profile URL. Full sweep green: tsc 0 errors, vitest 55 files / 511 tests, eslint 0 errors, verify-schema 18/18, test:e2e 15/15, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT VERIFIED: no real unfurl. Facebook, iMessage and Slack cannot reach this sandbox, so criterion 3's "from a phone" is verified as its two halves — the share button produces a ?listing= URL (e2e), and that URL renders the property's photo and address to a crawler (curl) — not as an observed message bubble. Cloudflare's own routing (that /jane reaches the function before the _redirects fallback) is likewise untested here; CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOYMENT.md now documents the binding the function needs and the curl that confirms it in production.

userStories.title: Analytics counters: unthrottled view and click increments, no tracking on page-builder pages, and contact taps the agent never sees
userStories.description: usePublicProfile.ts:59-68 calls increment_profile_views, a SECURITY DEFINER RPC with no throttle (baseline:1806-1814), from the anon client; the analytics_views throttle from US-092 does not cover profiles.view_count, so the headline number and the analytics rows diverge and anyone can loop it. increment_link_clicks has no throttle either. An agent with a custom page gets the full profile fetch and both increments (FullProfilePage.tsx:49-85) and is then redirected to /p/, where PublicPage.tsx tracks nothing, so page-builder users have no analytics. Call, Email and Text taps are only logger.info'd (FullProfilePage.tsx:424), so the agent never learns that 30 people tapped Call this week.
acceptanceCriteria: profiles.view_count is derived from throttled analytics_views inserts (a trigger) or the RPC applies the same per-visitor limit; increment_link_clicks gets an equivalent limit
PublicPage.tsx records views through the same path as FullProfilePage, and the redirect no longer double-counts
Call, email and text taps insert an analytics event and the dashboard Analytics page shows contact taps alongside link clicks
The Analytics page states the counters are indicative (visitor ids are client-generated)
userStories.notes:
Done. All four criteria met, verified against a live Postgres and a real browser.

(1) THE COUNTERS. profiles.view_count came from increment_profile_views, a SECURITY DEFINER RPC with no throttle at all, called from the anon client — while the analytics_views rows it was supposed to agree with had US-092's 30/minute per-visitor ceiling. So the headline number and the chart measured different things by construction, and anyone holding the anon key (it ships in the bundle) could loop the RPC and inflate any agent's headline without limit. Migration 20260902000012 hangs an AFTER INSERT trigger off analytics_views instead, so the counter inherits the throttle and cannot diverge; the client no longer calls the RPC.
Reproduced and verified by execution: 60 inserts from one visitor leave analytics_views at 30 rows AND view_count at 30. Before, the RPC ran unbounded next to a throttled table.

REVOKE FROM PUBLIC, not from anon. The first attempt was `REVOKE ... FROM anon, authenticated` and `SET ROLE anon; SELECT increment_profile_views(...)` still succeeded and still bumped the counter — Postgres grants EXECUTE on a new function to PUBLIC by default, and revoking from the two role names leaves that default in place. Caught by running the probe, not by reading the migration.

increment_link_clicks had the same absence of any bound. It now takes a visitor_id (the one-argument version had to be dropped rather than overloaded — a one-argument call would match both and Postgres rejects that as ambiguous) and applies the same 30/minute limit. 60 calls leave click_count at 30.

(2) THE PAGE-BUILDER BLIND SPOT. An agent with a custom page got the full profile fetch and a view recorded against their profile, then a redirect to /p/<slug>, which tracked nothing whatever. The page their visitors actually saw had no analytics and the page nobody saw got the view. PublicPage now uses the same useProfileTracking hook, and FullProfilePage waits for the custom-page check to settle before tracking, so one visit is one view either way. Also removed the increment from usePublicProfile entirely: fetching a profile is not a view, and it ran even for a profile that immediately redirects.

(3) CONTACT TAPS. Call, Email and Text were logger.info'd on the visitor's own console and nowhere else. New table analytics_events (link_click, contact_call, contact_email, contact_text) with the same open-insert-plus-throttle shape as analytics_views, but a tighter policy: the INSERT requires the target profile to be published, so it cannot be used to write rows against private accounts. Verified as anon: an insert on a published profile is accepted, the same insert against an unpublished one is rejected by RLS, and anon reads back nothing.
Both contact surfaces are wired — ContactButtons and StickyActionBar, which is the primary one on a phone and reported nothing at all, not even to the console. trackLinkClick now writes a dated event too, because links.click_count is a lifetime total and cannot answer "this month".
The dashboard's "Recent Activity" card — which printed the total view count again under a different heading — is replaced by Taps & Clicks: taps by method, total link clicks, and the top five links. The CSV export carries them too; it omitted them before because nothing recorded them.

(4) THE COUNTERS ARE CALLED INDICATIVE, in a line under the cards and in the export. visitor_id is generated in the visitor's own browser and stored in localStorage: clearing it counts one person twice, and automation can inflate a total. The rate limits bound that; they do not eliminate it, and the page now says so rather than presenting the numbers as measurement.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- verify-schema gains "view and click counters are throttled, and match the rows they count" — 19 checks. Each of the three defects was reintroduced in the live database and the check went red on each: dropping the trigger gives "analytics_views has 30 rows but profiles.view_count is 0"; re-granting the RPC to anon gives "anon can still call increment_profile_views"; removing the click throttle gives "60 link clicks from one visitor in a minute".
- The check is idempotent: it deletes its own rate_limit_entries rows first. Without that it failed on a second run inside the same minute — and, worse, passed vacuously, because 0 rows and a 0 counter are equal and under the ceiling. Confirmed by running verify-schema three times back to back.
- Note for the record: verify-schema does NOT replay migrations, it queries an already-migrated database. Editing a migration file proves nothing about it. The replay was checked separately, the way CI does it: a fresh database, the prelude, then all 24 migrations in filename order — clean, 148 tables, verify-schema 19/19 and types.ts in sync against it.
- types.ts regenerated from the applied schema (135 tables, 81 functions); types:check is green.
- 12 new unit tests (analyticsEvents, useProfileTracking) and 3 e2e specs (tests/e2e/analytics-tracking.spec.ts), which assert the requests, because the requests are what changed: one analytics_views insert per visit, zero calls to increment_profile_views, exactly one view for an agent whose profile redirects to a page-builder page, and a contact_call event on a Call tap. All three go red on the original code.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 57 files / 523 tests, eslint 0 errors, validate-migrations 24/24, verify-schema 19/19, test:e2e 18/18, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT VERIFIED / NOTED
- Existing profiles.view_count values are left as they are. They were inflated by an unthrottled RPC over an unknown period and analytics_views does not hold the full history, so there is no honest number to reconcile them to. From this migration forward the two agree; before it they do not, and no backfill can fix that.
- Found on the way, not fixed: PublicPage reads theme.colors.primary directly, so a custom page whose theme is partial or empty crashes into the error boundary. The page builder always writes a full theme, so this is not reachable today — but it is one bad row away. Belongs with US-116, which is about the page builder.

userStories.title: One public page, not two: the page builder silently replaces the listings profile, autosaves in a loop, and collides on slugs
userStories.description: FullProfilePage.tsx:48-82,157-158 queries custom_pages on every profile view and <Navigate to='/p/...'> if the agent has any active published page, so building a page in the page builder replaces the entire listings and lead-capture profile. DemoProfilesShowcase.tsx:107 links /p/${username}, which 404s unless the slug equals the username. PageList.tsx:71 creates every page with slug = username and there is no slug editor (PageBuilder.tsx:355-361 edits only title), so a second page fails on custom_pages_user_id_slug_key with 'Failed to save page'; PublicPage.tsx:105-109 looks slugs up globally (.eq('slug').single()) so two agents with the same slug break each other; setAsActivePage (pageBuilderStore.ts:437-443) never clears other actives and the .single() checks then fail. PageBuilder.tsx:133-145's autosave effect depends on isSaving, which savePage flips, so the editor writes and toasts 'Page saved successfully' every three seconds for as long as it is open.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide and implement one public surface: page-builder blocks render as sections inside FullProfilePage (recommended), or pages live at /:username/:pageSlug with the redirect and the /p/ route removed
Autosave fires only when the serialised page differs from the last saved version, and only callers toast
New pages get unique slugs, the slug is editable, lookups are scoped to the user, and setAsActivePage deactivates siblings
DemoProfilesShowcase links resolve; an e2e spec visits a demo profile and a page-builder page
npx tsc --noEmit reports 0 errors
userStories.notes:
Done. All five criteria met.

(1) THE DECISION: page-builder blocks are a SECTION of /:username, the option the story recommends. Taken as the PRD's own call, not mine.
What it replaces: FullProfilePage queried custom_pages on every view and, if the agent had ANY active published page, returned <Navigate to="/p/<slug>">. So opening the page builder once and marking a page active silently took that agent's listings, sold properties, testimonials, contact buttons, links and lead capture off the public web — and the /p/ page that replaced them recorded no analytics (US-115) and carried none of the profile's social metadata (US-114). The only way back was to find and deactivate the page.
Now: usePublicProfile fetches the active page alongside everything else (maybeSingle + limit(1) — .single() raises PGRST116 for none AND for several), and CustomBlocksSection renders its blocks under the testimonials. The blocks inherit the profile's theme, header, tracking and unfurl rather than needing a second set of each.
/p/:slug survives as a compatibility redirect for links already shared: it resolves the owner and sends them to /:username, 404ing anything unresolvable. The 325-line second renderer is gone — keeping it would have left two ways to render blocks, which is the thing this story is about. Note the /p/ lookup was ALWAYS ambiguous: custom_pages is unique on (user_id, slug), not on slug, so `.eq('slug').single()` broke for both agents whenever two shared one. The shim takes the most recently updated match, which is honest for an address that is no longer public.

(2) AUTOSAVE. The effect depended on isSaving, which savePage flips true then false — so every save re-ran the effect, which scheduled another save. The editor wrote to the database and toasted "Page saved successfully" every three seconds for as long as it was open. It now depends on pageSnapshot(page) and returns early when that equals lastSavedSnapshot, so a save cannot retrigger itself; the snapshot deliberately excludes updatedAt, which would otherwise make every page look dirty the instant it was saved — the same loop by another route. savePage no longer toasts at all; only the Save and Publish buttons do. Autosave also skips while the slug is mid-edit, so a keystroke cannot produce "Failed to save page".

(3) SLUGS. Every page was created with slug = username, so the second page collided on custom_pages_user_id_slug_key and the editor said "Failed to save page" — with no slug field anywhere to change it in, because the meta editor exposed only the title. New: src/lib/pageSlug.ts (slugify / uniqueSlug / validateSlug, with a reserved-word list), PageList suffixes to the first free slug, and the builder toolbar has a labelled address field that normalises as you type and shows what the constraint would say. savePage's existence check is scoped by user_id and uses maybeSingle — it was `.single()` with the error destructured away, so "does this page exist" was answered by a swallowed PGRST116. setAsActivePage now clears the siblings first: it only ever set is_active and never unset it, so an agent who activated a second page had two active rows and the .single() lookups that ask which page is active failed for both.
ProfileDisplaySettings had the same .single() on the active page and its own unscoped update; both fixed, and its copy no longer offers a choice between two profiles that no longer exists.

(4) DEMO LINKS. DemoProfilesShowcase linked /p/${username} — a page-builder slug — which 404'd for every agent whose page slug was not exactly their username, which was most of them. It links /${username} now. The dashboard's two "View"/"Preview" buttons pointed at /p/<slug> as well and now point at the real public address.

(5) tsc --noEmit: 0 errors.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- 4 e2e specs (tests/e2e/page-builder-surface.spec.ts): a page-builder page adds to the profile instead of replacing it (the agent's name, their listing AND the block text all on /:username, with the URL unchanged); a profile without one is unchanged; an already-shared /p/ link lands on the profile; the demo showcase links to a profile.
- 7 unit tests across pageSnapshot and pageBuilderStore, plus 11 for pageSlug.
- Every guard proved red on the original code: restoring the Navigate fails two of the four e2e specs; restoring the /p/ demo link fails the fourth; removing the sibling clear, the snapshot and the user_id scope fails all four store tests.
- One of the four was vacuous when first written and was fixed: the demo-link spec passed even with the /p/ link restored, because the profiles catch-all returns [] and the showcase did not render at all — "no /p/ links" is trivially true of an empty page. It now mocks a profile, asserts the card is visible, and asserts its href.
- Also updated US-115's analytics spec, which asserted the redirect this story removes. Its intent is unchanged and stronger: one page, one view.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 60 files / 541 tests, eslint 0 errors, verify-schema 19/19, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT DONE / NOTED
- No migration. custom_pages is unchanged; every fix here is in the client. A global UNIQUE on slug would be the belt-and-braces version but would break existing rows that legitimately collide across agents.
- src/lib/seo.ts still builds /p/<slug> URLs in generatePersonSchema and generateRealEstateAgentSchema. Both are uncalled anywhere in src/, so they emit nothing today; they are dead code for US-124 rather than a live wrong URL.
- Block animations and the floating CTA that PublicPage had are not carried over. The profile has its own presentation, and reproducing a second one is what this story removes.

userStories.title: Settings page shows fake billing to every agent, edits the username unsafely, and caches the profile under the wrong shape
userStories.description: Settings.tsx:583-606 renders 'Professional - $49/month', card '4242' and 'February 15, 2024' as literals with Manage/Update/View Invoices buttons that have no handlers; a free-plan agent reads that they are paying $49 with a card on file. Profile.tsx:308-319 is a plain required <input name='username'> sent raw by handleSubmit, while Settings.tsx:272-276 uses UsernameInput with lowercasing and an availability check: two editors, one unsafe. The public lookup (usePublicProfile.ts:51) is case-sensitive, so 'JohnSmith' saved from Profile is reachable only at /JohnSmith, unique-key collisions surface as 'Failed to update profile', and nothing warns that every printed card breaks. useUsernameCheck.ts:33-37 queries profiles as anon, which since 20260808000002 sees only published rows, so a username held by an unpublished profile reads 'available'. acceptanceCriteria: The billing block reads useSubscription() and links to /dashboard/subscription, or is removed
One username editor remains, lowercases, validates, checks availability through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that sees unpublished profiles, and confirms 'existing links will break' before saving
Settings uses useProfile(); no second ['profile'] query exists
Vitest covers the username RPC and the Settings profile query
userStories.notes:
Done. All four criteria met.

(1) THE BILLING BLOCK was four literals: "Professional - $49/month", "•••• •••• •••• 4242", "February 15, 2024", and three buttons (Manage Plan / Update / View Invoices) with no onClick at all. An agent on the free plan read that they were paying $49 a month with a card on file, and pressing anything did nothing to correct them. It reads useSubscription() now: the real plan name or "Free", the real renewal date when there is one, and a Link to /dashboard/subscription. Payment method and invoices are not restated — they live in Stripe's billing portal, and restating them would mean inventing them again.

(2) ONE USERNAME EDITOR. Profile.tsx had a plain required <input name="username"> whose value handleSubmit sent raw; Settings had UsernameInput, which lowercases, validates and checks availability. Two editors, one unsafe. Profile's is read-only now, with a link to Settings, and its submit strips the field so the form cannot send it. The surviving path lowercases and trims in the mutation as well as the input, runs validateUsername, and asks the RPC before writing — a collision used to reach the case-sensitive unique index and surface as a bare "Failed to update profile" naming no field.
Renaming now asks first. An AlertDialog names both addresses and says every link already shared — printed cards, the Instagram bio, past emails — will stop working, and that the old address is not kept. Nothing is written until the agent confirms; a save that does not change the username still saves without a prompt.

(3) THE AVAILABILITY CHECK. useUsernameCheck queried `profiles` directly as the current (often anon) user, and since 20260808000002 the public SELECT policy on that table is scoped to published rows. So a username held by an unpublished profile — every account that has not published yet, which includes every account mid-signup — came back as no row and the field said "Username is available".
Reproduced against the live database before fixing: with an unpublished profile holding 'hiddenagent', `SET ROLE anon; SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE username='hiddenagent'` returns 0, while check_username_available('hiddenagent') returns false. The hook calls the RPC now.
Migration 20260902000013 makes that RPC usable everywhere the question is asked: _current_user_id gets a DEFAULT NULL (it was required, which is part of why the client went round it) and the comparison becomes IS DISTINCT FROM — with a NULL current user, `id != NULL` is NULL for every row, so the EXISTS found nothing and EVERY username would have read as available. It also pins the full search_path: it had `SET search_path TO 'public'`, which leaves pg_temp searched first inside a SECURITY DEFINER function, so a caller could shadow `profiles` with a temp table.

(4) SETTINGS USES useProfile(). It declared its own useQuery on ['profile', user.id] returning the raw row, while useProfile returns toProfile(data) with the phone decrypted — two queryFns under one key, the same cache collision US-094 fixed on ['leads']. Whichever mounted first decided the shape the other saw, so Profile.tsx could render ciphertext in the phone field after a visit to Settings. There is now one query.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- 12 new unit tests: useUsernameCheck (6) asserts the RPC is called and the table is NOT — the mocked client throws if anything calls .from() — plus the unpublished-holder case, the signup case with no current user, format rejection short-circuiting the RPC, and a failed check reading as not-available rather than as a green light. Settings (6) covers the billing block, the profile query and the rename confirmation.
- All seven relevant guards proved red on the original code: restoring the literal "$49/month", the direct save without confirmation, and the direct profiles query fails 7 of 12.
- verify-schema gains "check_username_available sees profiles the anon client cannot" — 20 checks. It asserts the premise too (that anon really cannot see the row), so it cannot pass vacuously if the policy changes. Confirmed red: ALTER FUNCTION ... SECURITY INVOKER gives "says a taken username is free" and "is case-sensitive; the unique index is not".
- The RPC call was first written with a conditional spread, and verify-schema printed "uses a spread or computed key — not checked". Rewritten as a literal object with `_current_user_id: currentUserId ?? undefined` (JSON drops undefined, so the default still applies) so the argument-name check actually covers it.
- Migrations replayed from empty the way CI does: fresh database, prelude, 25 migrations in order — clean, verify-schema 20/20, types.ts in sync.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 62 files / 553 tests, eslint 0 errors, validate-migrations 25/25, verify-schema 20/20, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT DONE / NOTED
- Nothing migrates existing mixed-case usernames. The public lookup matches the column exactly, so a 'JohnSmith' saved by the old Profile editor is still reachable only at /JohnSmith. Lowercasing them would silently move those agents' public addresses, which is exactly what this story adds a confirmation dialog to prevent — it is the agent's call, not a migration's.
- src/lib/edgeFunctions.ts still exposes a check-username edge function wrapper. Nothing calls it; it is dead code for US-124 rather than a second live path.

userStories.title: Billing: the dashboard upgrade sends placeholder Stripe price ids, pricing copy contradicts the config, and a scheduled cancel drops the agent to Free today
userStories.description: SubscriptionPage.tsx:89 uses plan.stripe_price_id_monthly from src/config/pricing-plans.ts:151-152, which are the literals 'price_starter_monthly' / 'price_starter_yearly'; create-checkout-session only checks /^price_/, so Stripe replies 'No such price' and the agent sees 'Could not start checkout'. Pricing.tsx already uses stripePriceIdFor over the subscription_plans rows, but no migration seeds that table, so a fresh environment renders an empty pricing grid, and stripe-webhook/index.ts:116-162 keeps a third copy of the limits (analytics 7 days vs 30 in config). Pricing.tsx:401 and its JSON-LD at :121 say Starter $19, Professional $39, Team $29 per agent with a 5-agent minimum; the card at 282-284 repeats 'per agent (5 minimum)'; Landing.tsx:34 says '$39/month'; the config says 29/49/99 flat and checkout sends quantity 1. Pricing.tsx:357's Free CTA links to /register, which does not exist and falls into /:slug as 'profile not found'; VsLater.tsx:107,740 link /get-started and :113 /demo, neither routed. stripe-webhook:306-308 writes status 'canceled' the day cancel_at_period_end is set and get_user_plan (baseline:1560) joins only status='active', so a paid-up agent loses Pro features immediately; invoice.payment_failed to past_due has the same effect with no grace.
acceptanceCriteria: SubscriptionPage uses useSubscription().plans and stripePriceIdFor(plan, interval) with a monthly/yearly toggle; the placeholder ids are deleted from config
A migration seeds subscription_plans and the webhook and frontend config read limits from it (or CI generates the config from it); one source of truth
FAQ, JSON-LD and landing copy render prices from the plan rows; the per-agent claim is removed or seat quantity is implemented end to end
All links on Pricing, Landing and VsLater resolve to routes in App.tsx, checked by a test that greps to= and href= against the route table
A subscription with cancel_at_period_end stays active until current_period_end, and past_due keeps access for a stated grace window; both covered by webhook unit tests
userStories.notes:
Done. All five criteria met.

(1) CHECKOUT COULD NEVER HAVE WORKED. SubscriptionPage read plan.stripe_price_id_monthly from src/config/pricing-plans.ts, whose values were the literals 'price_starter_monthly' and friends — strings that are not price ids in any Stripe account. create-checkout-session only checks /^price_/, so they passed validation and Stripe answered "No such price", which reached the agent as "Could not start checkout". The page now reads useSubscription().plans and stripePriceIdFor(plan, interval), with a monthly/yearly toggle — annual prices were in the rows all along and there was no way to buy one, because the button always sent the monthly id. A plan with no configured price is disabled and says so, rather than failing at the till. The literals are deleted from the config, and a test asserts none come back.

(2) ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Nothing had ever seeded subscription_plans — 0 rows. Pricing.tsx reads it, so a fresh environment rendered an empty pricing grid; get_user_plan joins it, so every agent fell through to its hard-coded fallback. Meanwhile three other places each held their own copy, and they disagreed (config: analytics 30 days on free; webhook getPlanLimits: 7 days; Pricing copy: an entirely different price list).
Migration 20260902000014 seeds the table and makes it the authority. It needed a UNIQUE constraint on `name` first — there wasn't one, which also means get_user_plan's `WHERE name = 'free'` SELECT ... INTO would raise on duplicates. The Stripe price ids are deliberately left NULL: they are environment-specific and belong to the Stripe account, and the ON CONFLICT clause does not touch them, so re-running cannot wipe what an operator filled in.
The webhook's getPlanLimits table is gone; loadPlanLimits() reads the row. Its fallback is now the FREE limits, not 'professional' — the old `limits[planName] || limits.professional` handed out the paid tier on a lookup miss.
Two more defects found while doing this, both of which meant a paying agent was on the free plan:
  - the plan lookup matched `stripe_price_id` alone, the pre-interval column, which is NULL on every seeded row. So plan_id came back undefined, user_subscriptions stored NULL, and get_user_plan's JOIN found nothing from the moment checkout completed. It now matches any of the three price-id columns.
  - customer.subscription.updated never wrote plan_id at all, so an agent who changed plan in the billing portal kept the entitlements of the plan they left.

(3) THE COPY. The JSON-LD and the FAQ each carried their own sentence saying "Starter ($19/month), Professional ($39/month), and Team ($29/agent/month with 5 agent minimum)" — while the cards beside them rendered 29/49/99 from the rows this page already reads. Both now render one sentence derived from the plan rows. The per-agent claim is removed rather than implemented: nothing counts seats, the plan row is a flat price and checkout sends quantity 1, so a per-seat product on the page an agent buys from is a billing promise the system cannot keep. Stale prices on Landing ($39), VsBeacons ($39), VsLinktree ($39) and VsLater ($19, and a $44 total) corrected to the real 29/49.
src/config/pricing-plans.test.ts parses the seed SQL and asserts the config's plan names, prices, listing caps and analytics retention match it — so the remaining frontend copy cannot drift from the table again silently.

(4) LINKS. src/routes.test.ts parses App.tsx's route table (a brace-depth scan, because several routes span multiple lines and the element={…} expressions contain '>' of their own) and every literal to= / href= in src/, 157 links. It excludes /:slug and /* deliberately: the profile catch-all matches any single segment, which is exactly how /register reached "profile not found" instead of a 404, and /* is NotFound. It found precisely the four broken links the story names — /register on Pricing, /get-started twice and /demo on VsLater — and now guards the next one. Fixed to /auth/register and /for-real-estate-agents.

(5) CANCELLATION AND DUNNING. stripe-webhook did `if (cancel_at_period_end) status = 'canceled'`, and get_user_plan joined `WHERE us.status = 'active'` — so the day an agent scheduled a cancellation they dropped to the free plan, losing weeks they had paid for. cancel_at_period_end is a separate boolean the webhook was already storing correctly; rewriting the status threw the distinction away. past_due had the same effect with no grace, so a card that expired on a Tuesday cut off access on the Tuesday, before Stripe had finished retrying.
The webhook stores Stripe's status unchanged (statusToStore), and 20260902000015 makes get_user_plan follow what was paid for: active/trialing, or canceled while current_period_end is in the future, or past_due within 7 days of it. Verified by execution against the live database — cancelled+paid-through -> professional; cancelled+period over -> free; past_due 2 days -> professional; past_due 10 days -> free.
Caught by running it: the first version compared `us.status IN ('canceled','cancelled')`. subscription_status is an enum whose only label is 'canceled', and the two-l spelling raises "invalid input value for enum" at RUN time, not at CREATE FUNCTION time — so the function would have compiled fine and thrown on every call.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- 7 webhook unit tests (supabase/functions/_shared/subscription-entitlement.test.ts) over the extracted decisions: a scheduled cancellation does not become a cancelled subscription, Stripe's status passes through, the paid-through and grace boundaries hold, and anything unrecognised fails closed.
- verify-schema gains "subscription entitlement survives a scheduled cancellation" — 21 checks. Proved red twice against the live database: restoring the active-only join gives "a cancellation scheduled for 20 days' time already reads as free" and "a payment that failed 2 days ago already reads as free; there is no grace"; emptying subscription_plans gives "holds 0 active row(s); the seed did not run".
- Migrations replayed from empty as CI does: fresh database, prelude, 27 migrations in order — clean, verify-schema 21/21, types in sync.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 65 files / 568 tests, eslint 0 errors, validate-migrations 27/27, verify-schema 21/21, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT VERIFIED / NOTED
- No Stripe call was made. There is no Stripe account, key or webhook secret here, so checkout, the billing portal and the webhook's HTTP path are untested end to end; what is tested is the logic they run on.
- deno check did not run — Deno is not installed in this sandbox. The edge-function changes are type-checked in CI only. The extracted _shared module has no Deno globals at module scope, so its tests do run under vitest.
- The seeded rows carry no Stripe price ids, so no plan is purchasable until an operator fills them in per environment (scripts/setup-stripe-products.sh, or by hand). That is the honest state: it was previously 'purchasable' only in the sense that the button existed.

userStories.title: Backend authorization gaps: an unauthenticated SSRF proxy, an open email relay, account lockout by anyone, a workflow IDOR, and unguarded webhook fetches
userStories.description: test-article-webhook/index.ts:11,56,86-92 has no auth, POSTs to a body-supplied webhookUrl and echoes the response status and body; on self-hosted Supabase the edge runtime shares a Docker network with postgres-meta, Kong and GoTrue, so this is a full unauthenticated internal read. publish-article-to-social/index.ts:195 fetches stored article_webhooks.webhook_url with no guard. send-welcome-email/index.ts:14-35 takes to/name/username from the body with no auth or limit: an AgentBio-branded relay from noreply@agentbio.net to any address with any link. login-security/index.ts:37-60,119-140,160-180 has no auth: five POSTs of {action:'record_attempt', email, success:false} lock any account for 30 minutes, and register_session inserts a user_sessions row for any userId. execute-workflow/index.ts:277-290 loads workflow_executions by executionId with the service-role client and never compares user.id, so any user can run anyone's workflow. submit-lead/index.ts:182 fetches the agent-controlled zapier_webhook_url with no SSRF guard, ZapierIntegrationModal.tsx:38-40 writes it unvalidated and there is no CHECK on the column, so an agent can aim it at http://postgres-meta:8080. pii-crypto/index.ts:66-118 decrypts up to 200 arbitrary ciphertexts for any JWT, and audit_table_change (baseline:102-155) stores to_jsonb(NEW) for leads and profiles, so audit_logs holds every ciphertext and every Zapier URL for that oracle to decrypt.
acceptanceCriteria: test-article-webhook requires admin, validates the URL with ssrf-guard and does not echo the response body; publish-article-to-social guards its fetch the same way
send-welcome-email requires a JWT and takes the address from user.email and the username from the profile
record_attempt and register_session require the service role (or are driven from a GoTrue hook); check_throttle remains public and is rate limited by IP
execute-workflow rejects an execution whose workflow.user_id is not the caller
zapier_webhook_url is validated with isValidWebhookUrl on write and guarded with ssrf-guard on fetch, and a CHECK constraint limits it to hooks.zapier.com and hook.*.make.com

npm run test:security covers each of the six endpoints
userStories.notes:
Done. All seven criteria met.

(1) THE UNAUTHENTICATED PROXY. test-article-webhook had no auth at all: it took a URL from the request body, POSTed to it, and returned the response status AND body. On self-hosted Supabase the edge runtime shares a Docker network with postgres-meta, Kong and GoTrue, so anyone who could reach the function could read those services and get the answer back. Three changes, all needed: requireAdmin (it is an operator tool), the destination allow-list plus safeFetch (which resolves the host, refuses private and reserved ranges, and re-checks every redirect hop — a public hostname that redirects to 127.0.0.1 defeats a single up-front check), and the response body is no longer read or returned at all. Echoing a body is what made it a read primitive; the status answers the question the operator is actually asking. publish-article-to-social's fetch of the stored webhook_url is guarded the same way — stored is not the same as trusted when the form that wrote it validated nothing.

(2) THE OPEN RELAY. send-welcome-email took `to`, `full_name` and `username` from an unauthenticated body: an AgentBio-branded email from noreply@agentbio.net to any address, with any name and a link to any path on the site. Nothing about the message is caller-supplied now — the address comes from auth.users via the verified JWT, the name and profile URL from that user's own profile row. The onboarding caller sends an empty body.

(3) LOCKOUT BY ANYONE. Five POSTs of {action:'record_attempt', email, success:false} locked any account for thirty minutes, because check_login_throttle counted an email's failures across EVERY source address. Reproduced against the live database: five failures from 10.0.0.1 left the owner at 203.0.113.9 blocked.
record_attempt stays callable without a session — a FAILED login has no session, and recording failures is the whole point of the control — but 20260902000016 scopes the per-account counter to the caller's own address, so an unauthenticated caller can now only lock out the machine they are using. A real brute force from one address is still stopped at five (verified). The endpoint is rate limited by address on every action, and record_attempt no longer attributes an attempt to a body-supplied user id.
register_session now takes the owner from the JWT and ignores the body's userId — it used to insert a user_sessions row for any account, which is both a forged audit trail and a way to fill someone's active-sessions list.
Found while doing this: the function had `p_ip_address inet` and the original body compared it to a text parameter in my first draft, which Postgres accepted at CREATE time and raised on at CALL time. It also revealed that declaring the parameter `text` creates a second overload rather than replacing the function.

(4) THE WORKFLOW IDOR. execute-workflow loaded workflow_executions with the SERVICE-ROLE client — so RLS did not apply — and never compared user.id. Any authenticated user could pass any executionId and run someone else's workflow, with their variables and their integrations, writing the results onto their execution record. Being logged in was the only requirement. It now refuses, answering "not found" rather than "forbidden": whether an execution id exists is not something a stranger should learn.

(5) THE ZAPIER URL. Three layers now agree where there were none: a CHECK constraint on the column (https, and only hooks.zapier.com or hook.<region>.make.com), isValidWebhookUrl plus safeFetch in submit-lead, and src/lib/webhookUrl.ts in the modal so the agent is told what is wrong instead of meeting the constraint as "Failed to save webhook URL". Verified against the live database: http://postgres-meta:8080/tables is rejected by the column; Zapier and Make URLs are accepted. Rows already outside the list are cleared by the migration rather than left behind. isValidWebhookUrl also now requires https (a webhook carries lead PII to a third party) and accepts any Make region — it hard-coded us1 and eu1, silently rejecting agents elsewhere.

(6) THE DECRYPTION ORACLE. pii-crypto's `decrypt` took up to 200 arbitrary ciphertexts and returned plaintext to any valid JWT, with no check that the caller could ever have read those rows. That mattered because audit_table_change stores to_jsonb(NEW) for `leads` and `profiles`, so audit_logs held a copy of every ciphertext and every zapier_webhook_url ever written — anything that obtained one could bring it here to be opened.
Decryption is addressed by row id now: decrypt_leads takes lead ids and filters to `.eq('user_id', user.id)`, decrypt_profile takes nothing at all and reads the caller's own row. There is no longer any way to hand the function a ciphertext. Encryption still takes values, which is not an oracle.
20260902000017 redacts before serialising: encrypted_*, zapier_webhook_url, webhook_url, session_token_hash, *_secret and *api_key* are replaced with "[redacted]" rather than removed, so an audit reader can still see that a field changed. Verified by execution — the audit row no longer holds the ciphertext or the webhook URL, and still names the lead.

(7) TEST COVERAGE. tests/security/edge-authz.security.spec.ts covers all seven endpoints and every one was proved red by removing its own guard (5 of 7 on the first pass; the other two were confirmed separately). These are SOURCE assertions and I want that on the record: there is no Deno runtime and no Supabase instance here or in CI, so nothing proves the DEPLOYED function refuses a request. What they catch is a guard being deleted, which is the failure mode that actually happens. The behavioural half is real: 18 validation tests, 7 webhookUrl tests, 13 pii tests (including that the client never sends a ciphertext), and a verify-schema check.

npm run test:security COULD NOT RUN AT ALL before this. Its webServer used `npm run dev` without --host 127.0.0.1, and vite defaults host to '::' — in any environment without IPv6 the dev server died with "listen EAFNOSUPPORT" and the whole suite errored before a spec ran. It also passed no VITE_SUPABASE_* env, the same blank-page defect found in the a11y and e2e configs. Fixed both; the suite now runs: 91 passed (70 pre-existing plus the 21 new), 3 skipped, 0 failed.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- verify-schema gains "audit logs redact secrets, lockout is per-address, webhooks are bounded" — 22 checks. Proved red with all three defects restored in the live database: 4 findings at once.
- Migrations replayed from empty as CI does: fresh database, prelude, 29 migrations — clean; types regenerated (82 functions) and in sync.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 66 files / 574 tests, eslint 0 errors, validate-migrations 29/29, verify-schema 22/22, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6, test:security green.

NOT VERIFIED / NOTED
- No edge function was executed. Deno is not installed here, so `deno check` did not run either; the functions are type-checked in CI only.
- The pii-crypto contract change is breaking for any caller outside this repository. All three in-repo readers (useLeads, useAnalytics, useProfile) were converted, and decryptPIIBatch/decryptPII are removed so a missed caller is a compile error rather than a silent failure.
- Redaction applies from this migration forward. audit_logs rows written BEFORE it still hold ciphertext and webhook URLs. Purging them is a data decision, not a migration's — but the oracle that made them dangerous is closed, so the ciphertext is now just ciphertext.

userStories.notes:
Done. All five criteria met.

(1) THE ADMIN TOOLING. dashboard/Analytics.tsx mounted @/components/admin/SearchAnalyticsDashboard — Google Search Console, GA4, Bing and Yandex OAuth connections — in a 'Search Analytics' tab of the AGENT-facing page, with no admin gate on it at all. That is the platform's own SEO tooling for agentbio.net; an agent has no use for it and no business connecting a search-console property through it. The tab is gone and it lives at /admin/search-analytics behind RequireAuth requireAdmin.

(2) THE ORPHAN PAGE, merged rather than deleted. src/pages/AnalyticsDashboard.tsx was 417 lines reachable only by typing its URL — nothing linked to it but route-announcer. Its conversion funnel, lead-source breakdown, insights panel and report builder are now tabs on dashboard/Analytics.tsx; the page and its route are removed.
Not carried over: a grid of four 'Available Reports' cards with cursor-pointer and no onClick at all, and the funnel's second stage. That stage was labelled 'Viewed Listing' and its only caller passed Math.round(uniqueVisitors * 0.7) — a number nothing measured, shown to the agent as measurement. calculateFunnel takes `engaged` now, and Analytics passes the real contact taps plus link clicks that analytics_events has recorded since US-115.

(3) THE NAV. Fifteen sidebar entries for a link-in-bio product aimed at people who are not technical, and MobileNav listed a DIFFERENT set — /dashboard/subscription, /team and /api-keys were in the sidebar and nowhere on mobile, so an agent on a phone could not reach their own billing. /dashboard/settings/delete-account had no link anywhere in the app.
src/config/dashboard-nav.ts is now the single source: seven primary destinations (Overview, Profile, Links, Listings, Leads, Analytics, Settings) and a SETTINGS_TOOLS list carrying Theme, Testimonials, Page Builder, Quick Actions, Workflows, Subscription, Team, API Keys and Delete Account. Both navs render from it, and the Settings page has a 'More tools' card linking every one — so nothing is orphaned, just no longer competing with the seven things an agent does daily.

(4) ONE GUARD, BOUNDARIES, LAZY. ProtectedRoute and SecureRoute were two components with different state machines writing the same lastVisitedRoute key; which one a route got was historical, and US-108's onboarding gate therefore applied only to the routes using ProtectedRoute. RequireAuth replaces both as a layout route with a requireAdmin prop — SecureRoute's only actual use, since every call site passed exactly that and nothing else. Both files are deleted.
Its admin branch waits while `role` is still null rather than refusing, or an admin gets a flash of 'Access denied' on every hard refresh; and it refuses in place rather than redirecting, because bouncing someone to /dashboard for a page they may not see reads as a broken link.
RouteErrorBoundary covered the dashboard, admin, the two tools and the two profile routes — and nothing else. The 13 public/legal/blog routes, 5 landings, 5 feature pages and 7 auth routes had none, so a render error on any of them was a white screen. PublicBoundary is a layout route wrapping all of them, so a page joins the group by nesting rather than by remembering to wrap it.
FullProfilePage was a static import: its twenty imports — listing modal, carousel, testimonials, theme engine — were in the entry chunk, downloaded by everyone who loaded the marketing site. It is lazy like every other page.
Also fixed: route-announcer named /dashboard/lead-management (removed by US-081) and /dashboard/analytics-advanced (deleted here), while /dashboard/subscription, /team and /api-keys had no entry at all.

(5) npm run test:e2e 22/22 and test:a11y 6/6 pass, both after the App.tsx restructure.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- 3 new test files, 21 tests: dashboard-nav (the config matches the route table, every dashboard route is reachable from a nav, neither nav hard-codes a /dashboard/ link), route-announcer (announces only routes that exist), and RequireAuth (12 tests including the onboarding gate, the not-yet-loaded profile, and all four admin cases).
- Proved red: removing Subscription/Team/API Keys/Delete Account from the config, reintroducing a hard-coded MobileNav link, and restoring the dead announcer entry fails 4 of 9.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 68 files / 589 tests, eslint 0 errors, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT VERIFIED / NOTED
- The entry-chunk saving from lazy-loading FullProfilePage is not measured here; `npm run build` bundle sizes belong to US-125, which is about exactly that.
- The seven-item nav follows the story's list literally. Testimonials, Page Builder and Quick Actions are not among the seven and are not named as moving to Settings either — they are in SETTINGS_TOOLS rather than being left unreachable, which is a judgement call worth flagging: Testimonials in particular is a content type like Listings and Links, and an argument could be made for promoting it back.

userStories.notes:
Done. All five criteria met. The root went from 194 entries to 57, and 121 markdown files to five.

(1) THE TEST THAT DIRTIED THE TREE. exportUtils.test.ts drove jsPDF's doc.save(), which under jsdom takes the Node path and wrote lead_report_<date>.pdf and performance_<date>.pdf into the repository ROOT on every `npm run test:run` — and four of them had been committed by accident (two of those by me, earlier in this loop).
jsPDF assigns `save` as an OWN property of each instance, not on the prototype, so the obvious fix does not work: vi.spyOn(jsPDF.prototype, 'save') fails with "The property save is not defined on the object". I found that by running it, not by reading. The test now mocks the module with a subclass whose constructor overwrites the own property after super(), so the whole render still runs and only the write is caught. A new test asserts the file does not exist on disk afterwards, and a full `vitest run` now leaves git status clean.

(2) REMOVED FROM THE TREE: test-reports/ (13 MB — a 9.5 MB JSON and 31 screenshots), db-backup/ (9.9 MB of cluster backups and article rows, of which .gitignore covered 2 of 14 files), public/logo.psd (2.7 MB), four PDFs, three CSVs, four .ps1 scripts, two .sh scripts, four import/update SQL files, migrations.zip, INSTALLING (0 bytes), ​.styleci.yml (a Laravel preset) and .claude/settings.local.json. 339,745 deleted lines.
.gitignore was rewritten: it had accumulated one-off filenames (Screenshot 2025-12-17 101035.png, AUTH_FIX_URGENT.md, quick-verify.ps1, .gitignore itself) alongside /vendor, Homestead.*, /public/hot and ​.phpunit.result.cache from the PHP project it was copied from. It now covers patterns — *.pdf, test-reports/, db-backup/, *.backup*, *.dump, the playwright report directories, .claude/settings.local.json — and nothing from Laravel.

(3) MARKDOWN. 116 files moved into docs/{setup,deploy,architecture,product,seo,reviews,archive}/; README, CLAUDE, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY and CODE_OF_CONDUCT stay in the root (there is no LICENSE.md in this repo). The archive is the honest home for the 29 point-in-time notes — SPRINT_*_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY, SESSION_SUMMARY, IMMEDIATE_FIX, SUCCESS.md and so on — which record what was true on a particular day; CLAUDE.md says so explicitly, because treating them as current is the trap.
The two CODE_REVIEW_2026-08.md files were not duplicates that drifted: one is the 606-line review, the other a 195-line status header plus a summary of the same pass. Reconciled by prepending the status block to the review and deleting the short copy.

(4) EARLIER PLATFORMS. src/types/linkstack.ts, LinkStackBlocks.tsx (imported by nothing), .lovable-rebuild, the lovable-tagger devDependency, its vite.config.ts plugin and the two [Lovable] log prefixes in main.tsx are gone. `npm run build` succeeds without the plugin.

(5) CLAUDE.md's internal-docs section is a table of the new locations, and the stale migrations paragraph is corrected: it claimed applying the migrations fails in ten places and that CI works around it with three passes. US-060's squashed baseline fixed that; the workflow runs one pass with ON_ERROR_STOP=1, over 29 files.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- src/repo-hygiene.test.ts, 10 tests: the root's markdown, no artifacts or dumps, no PDFs or CSVs, no loose scripts or SQL, the docs directories exist, one CODE_REVIEW_2026-08, the .gitignore patterns, no PHP entries, and no LinkStack/Lovable remnants. Proved red by dropping a stray .pdf, a .md, a .ps1 and a test-reports/ directory into the root: 4 of 10 fail.

- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 69 files / 600 tests, eslint 0 errors, validate-migrations 29/29, verify-schema 22/22, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6.

NOT DONE / NOTED
- History is not rewritten. The 23 MB of backups, reports and binaries are removed from the tree but remain in past commits, so `git clone` still pays for them. Rewriting history is a destructive, coordinated operation affecting anyone with a checkout — it is Dj's call, not a story's.
