userStories.title: One deployment path, one migration tree, one CI directory
userStories.description: Edge functions have four documented deployment paths: edge-functions-server.ts (unused; its FUNCTIONS_MAP lists 15 of 89 functions including the dead submit-contact), Dockerfile, edge-functions.Dockerfile, Dockerfile.gitclone, docker-compose.edge-functions.yml, nixpacks.toml, six COOLIFY_/EDGE_FUNCTIONS_/DOCKERFILE_ docs and two migrate-*.ps1 scripts. supabase/ holds all_migrations_combined.sql, all_migrations_safe.sql and migration_part_1..9.sql (1.3 MB) referenced by nothing; database/performance-indexes.sql says 'run these in the SQL editor' and 18 of its 23 indexes exist in no migration, so production indexes are unknowable from the repo; database/database.sqlite is an empty Laravel file. github-actions/ holds six workflow files GitHub never runs (only .github/workflows/ executes), its ci.yml differs from the live one by 350 lines, and cd/deploy/pr-preview/performance/security exist only there while GITHUB_ACTIONS_SETUP_COMPLETE.md documents them as done. mobile-native-js/ is a separate React Native app (32 files) nothing builds and tools/automated-testing/ (39 files) is a Playwright crawler whose only output is the committed test-reports/.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/deploy/edge-functions.md documents the one real path; the other Dockerfiles, the compose file, nixpacks.toml, edge-functions-server.ts and the .ps1 scripts are deleted
The 18 missing indexes are added in a migration (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS); database/, supabase/all_migrations_*.sql, supabase/migration_part_*.sql and migrations.zip are deleted
github-actions/ is deleted; any workflow from it that is wanted is moved into .github/workflows/ and runs green
mobile-native-js/ and tools/automated-testing/ are moved to their own repositories or deleted, with a note in docs/archive
npm run verify:migrations and the verify-backend workflow pass
userStories.notes:
Done. All five criteria met.

(1) ONE DEPLOYMENT PATH. Five build configurations — Dockerfile, edge-functions.Dockerfile, Dockerfile.gitclone, docker-compose.edge-functions.yml and nixpacks.toml — all shipped the same thing: edge-functions-server.ts, a hand-written Deno router with a FUNCTIONS_MAP listing 15 of the 86 functions in supabase/functions/.
Established by counting rather than by reading the docs: the app calls 34 distinct edge functions, and 25 of them are absent from that map — login-security, pii-crypto, submit-review, gdpr-deletion, create-portal-session, send-welcome-email among them. If that router were live, three quarters of the app's edge-function calls would 404 and login, lead decryption and billing would all be broken. They are not, so it cannot be what serves production. All five configurations, the router and .dockerignore are deleted.
docs/deploy/edge-functions.md documents the one real path: self-hosted Supabase's own edge runtime serving supabase/functions/ at /functions/v1/<name>, which is what VITE_FUNCTIONS_URL points at. It also records what was deleted and why, so the next person does not re-derive it. CLAUDE.md points there.

(2) THE INDEXES. database/performance-indexes.sql said "Run these in Supabase SQL Editor" and was referenced by nothing, so whether production had any of them depended on whether somebody had pasted the file into a console — the schema this repository describes and the schema queries run against could differ in every index.
20260902000018 adds 17 of them as a migration, all CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS so it is a no-op where they were pasted in by hand. Three of the file's statements are NOT carried over because they cannot run, which is itself evidence nobody had:
  - idx_articles_user_published indexed articles(user_id). There is no user_id on articles; it is author_id. Recreated correctly as idx_articles_author_published.
  - idx_analytics_views_recent and idx_leads_recent had `WHERE viewed_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'`. A partial index predicate must be immutable and NOW() is not, so Postgres rejects both with "functions in index predicate must be marked IMMUTABLE". Dropped rather than fixed: the unpartitioned (user_id, date DESC) indexes serve the same queries, and a rolling window in a predicate needs periodic rebuilding to stay useful.
database/ (including an empty Laravel database.sqlite), supabase/all_migrations_combined.sql, supabase/all_migrations_safe.sql and supabase/migration_part_1..9.sql — 1.3 MB referenced by nothing — are deleted. migrations.zip went in US-121.

(3) github-actions/ IS DELETED, and nothing was moved out of it. I read all six before deciding:
  - security.yml and performance.yml duplicate jobs the live ci.yml already has (npm audit at --audit-level=high, eslint, bundle-size).
  - cd.yml, deploy.yml and pr-preview.yml deploy to Cloudflare Pages from GitHub Actions. Cloudflare Pages already deploys from its own Git integration (docs/deploy/CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOYMENT.md), so adopting them would create a second deployment path — the exact thing this story removes.
  - ci.yml is a 350-line-divergent copy of the live one.
GitHub only executes .github/workflows/, so none of these had ever run, while GITHUB_ACTIONS_SETUP_COMPLETE.md documented them as done. That document is in docs/archive/.

(4) mobile-native-js/ (32 files, a React Native app sharing no code with src/ and referenced by no script) and tools/automated-testing/ (39 files, a Playwright crawler whose only output was the committed test-reports/) are deleted, with docs/archive/REMOVED_SUBPROJECTS.md recording what they were, the exact git commands to recover them, and why each belongs elsewhere. I could not move them to their own repositories — that needs an account decision and somewhere to put them — so deleting with the note is the honest half.

(5) npm run verify:migrations passes (30 files) and the verify-backend path passes: migrations replayed from empty into a fresh database in one pass with ON_ERROR_STOP=1, verify-schema 22/22 against it, types.ts in sync.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING
- 4 new tests in src/repo-hygiene.test.ts. Proved red by restoring Dockerfile, nixpacks.toml, github-actions/ and database/: 2 of 14 fail.
- npm run build succeeds without nixpacks.toml or any Dockerfile — the frontend build never used them.
- Full sweep: tsc 0 errors, vitest 69 files / 604 tests, eslint 0 errors, validate-migrations 30/30, verify-schema 22/22, test:e2e 22/22, test:a11y 6/6. The root is 46 entries.

NOT VERIFIED / NOTED
- I cannot see the Coolify service configuration, so I cannot prove no service points at a deleted Dockerfile. What I can prove is that any service built from one of them would be serving a router that answers 15 of the 34 functions the app calls — so if one exists it is already broken, and the docs claiming it as the deploy path were the defect. Worth confirming in Coolify before the next deploy.
- Whether production already has the 17 indexes is unknown from here; IF NOT EXISTS makes the migration safe either way, and from now on the repository is the record.

1. .env.example regenerated from a grep of import.meta.env.VITE_*. Out: seven VITE_FIREBASE_*, VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, and PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY — a server secret in a template whose every value is substituted into the shipped bundle. In: the eight names src/ read and nobody had written down. supabase/functions/.env.example is new: 34 names, each with a one-line purpose, plus the grep that regenerates it and a list of the retired spellings so they are not re-added. src/env-example.test.ts (7 assertions) reads the source rather than a snapshot, so both files drift into a failing test rather than into production; verified by adding a bogus name, deleting a real one and re-adding PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY — 7/7 failed, 7/7 passed on restore.

2. supabase/functions/_shared/env.ts exports getSiteUrl(), getFunctionsUrl() and getPagespeedApiKey(); 22 functions call them. SITE_URL/APP_URL/FRONTEND_URL/PUBLIC_SITE_URL, FUNCTIONS_URL/EDGE_FUNCTIONS_URL and PAGESPEED_API_KEY/PAGESPEED_INSIGHTS_API_KEY are gone from the tree — grep confirms zero remaining Deno.env.get of any retired name. Each helper trims, treats blank as unset and strips a trailing slash. env.test.ts asserts the retired names cannot win.

3. encrypt-pii deleted (ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY, raw 32-byte key, an envelope _shared/encryption.ts cannot read) and createAgentNotificationEmail/AGENT_EMAIL removed from _shared/email.ts. Both had zero callers — grepped the whole repo before deleting. _shared/encryption.ts's PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? ENCRYPTION_KEY fallback is KEPT and documented as deprecated in the new .env.example: both names feed the same algorithm, and I cannot see which is set on the live deployment. Dropping it would make MFA seeds and OAuth tokens undecryptable if production only sets ENCRYPTION_KEY.

4. The app URL now has one source. lib/utils.ts gained getConfiguredAppUrl() (the deployment's own address, for emailed links and redirect allowlists) beside getSafeOrigin() (the origin the visitor is on). config/seo.config.ts (hard-coded literal), lib/constants.ts, lib/structured-data.ts, lib/url-validation.ts and three inline copies of getSafeOrigin in SEOHead/PageSEO/FullProfilePage all go through it; seo.config's getBaseUrl is now a one-line delegate to getSafeOrigin, which it had been byte-for-byte duplicating. lib/instagram-bio-analyzer/email-templates.ts interpolated process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL — a Next.js name in a Vite app — into nine call-to-action links, so every one of them rendered as the literal text 'undefined/auth/register'. Fixed (the file itself has no importers; that is US-124's).

The GA id is out of public/scripts/analytics.js. It reads a <meta name="ga-measurement-id"> tag that a small vite plugin fills from VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID: a meta tag because analytics.js is a static asset with no import.meta.env and index.html's CSP is script-src 'self' with no unsafe-inline, so an inline script could not carry the value either; a plugin rather than Vite's own %VITE_%% substitution because that warns on every dev start and CI build when the variable is unset, which is the normal case outside production. Verified in a real Chromium against a built preview, both ways: id set -> meta 'G-TESTID123', gtag.js requested with that id, dataLayer length 3; id unset -> meta empty, no script injected, no request, dataLayer 0.

5. The seven static-CORS functions (get-sessions, revoke-session, login-security, audit-log, rate-limit, gdpr-export, gdpr-deletion) now call getCorsHeaders(origin) per request and handleCorsPreFlight for OPTIONS; the module-level `corsHeaders` export is deleted so it cannot come back. getCorsHeaders no longer answers '*' when there is no Origin header — it omits Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Allow-Credentials entirely, which is what a server-to-server caller needs (it reads neither). cors.test.ts covers it; restoring the '*' branch fails 2 of the 7, confirmed by sabotage-and-restore.

Also fixed, because it made verification impossible: playwright.config.ts's security-chrome project spread the PW_CHROMIUM_PATH executablePath into `use` and then overwrote the whole launchOptions key with the --disable-web-security args literal, so the override never applied and every spec in the project died at browserType.launch. Merged into one launchOptions. security-mobile is left alone with a comment: devices['iPhone 13'] is WebKit, which this container does not have, so no Chromium path helps it.

Verified by running: tsc --noEmit clean; vitest 72 files / 627 tests passed; verify:migrations 30 files OK; verify-schema all 22 checks pass against the live Postgres; production build clean with and without VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and with no Vite warning either way; esbuild parses every changed edge function and every relative import in them resolves to a real file; test:e2e 22 passed; test:a11y 6 passed.

NOT verified. The security suite could not be run to completion. Two blockers, both pre-existing and neither touched by this change: (a) the container ships Chromium build 1194 while the pinned Playwright wants 1200, so every project without an executablePath override fails at launch — the security-chrome half of that is fixed above, security-mobile needs WebKit; (b) the auth and password-reset specs POST to a Supabase that is not running here and hang or fail on rate-limit assertions. No security spec references Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so the CORS change is not what they exercise, but I did not prove that by running them. US-090 owns this suite.

Also NOT done, deliberately: the eslint config still gives public/**/*.js no browser globals, so analytics.js reports 13 no-undef errors where it reported 12 — my one added `document` reference. Same class as the existing twelve; US-125 owns the lint gate and should fix the config wholesale rather than have this story patch it.

Left for US-124: src/lib/constants.ts and src/lib/instagram-bio-analyzer/email-templates.ts have no importers anywhere in the repo. Both were fixed rather than deleted here, because deleting them is the dead-code sweep's call, not this story's.

userStories.title: Decide the fate of the SEO suite: 32 tables, 37 uncalled functions and 460 KB of admin UI that the agent never sees
userStories.description: Of 135 public tables, 32 are seo_* plus gsc_*, yandex_*, ga4_* and pseo_*; src/ queries 8 of the 32. Of 89 edge functions, 33 are invoked from src/ and 37 are referenced by nothing (analyze-*, check-*, crawl-site, detect-*, gsc-*, apply-seo-*, optimize-page-content, validate-structured-data, run-scheduled-audit and more), and no migration or workflow schedules any of them. 24 tables are touched by neither src/ nor supabase/functions (seo_automation_logs, seo_page_scores, seo_report_history, seo_settings, workflow_execution_queue, workflow_templates, workflow_triggers, workflow_versions, lead_scores, ml_training_examples, team_round_robin, rate_limits, mortgage_calculations, ...). src/components/admin is 460 KB across 33 components and SEODashboard.tsx is an 11-line wrapper around the same SEOManager that AdminDashboard.tsx:23 mounts as a tab. userStories.title: A person record: contacts that outlive a lead, deduplicated by email
userStories.description: A lead is the only person record in the product, and it is one-shot: one form submission is one leads row (supabase/functions/submit-lead/index.ts:126-140 inserts unconditionally, no lookup, no unique constraint). The same buyer asking about three listings is three strangers, and because email is ciphertext (encrypted_email, US-086) a duplicate cannot even be found by query — the Leads page searches email client-side over loaded pages only (src/pages/dashboard/Leads.tsx:427-430). An exhaustive search of src/ and supabase/ finds no contacts, clients or households table and no column for tags, birthday, anniversary, closing date, household details, preferred channel or 'past client'; preferred_contact_method exists only in the dead LegacyLead interface (src/types/lead.ts:48). leads.notes is never read or written. The user's ask — a buyer who becomes a past client whose birthday, home anniversary and family details keep them top of mind — has nowhere to live. This story adds the record; the pages that use it follow (US-129 to US-134).
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates contacts (id, user_id NOT NULL, first_name, last_name, encrypted_email, encrypted_phone, email_hash, phone_hash, stage CHECK IN ('lead','active_buyer','active_seller','past_client','sphere','archived') DEFAULT 'lead', tags text[] DEFAULT '{}', source, referred_by_contact_id self-FK, preferred_channel CHECK IN ('call','sms','email'), birthday date, current_address, personal_details jsonb, email_opt_in bool, sms_opt_in bool, do_not_contact bool DEFAULT false, last_contacted_at, next_touch_at, created_at, updated_at) and contact_important_dates (id, contact_id, user_id, label, date, recurs_annually bool DEFAULT true, remind_days_before int DEFAULT 7); both with RLS for the owner and for team assignees on the pattern of 20260902000006, updated_at triggers, indexes on (user_id, stage), (user_id, email_hash) and (user_id, next_touch_at)

email_hash and phone_hash are an HMAC-SHA256 of the normalised value keyed with the PII key, computed only server-side in _shared/encryption.ts (the key left the client in US-066); a unique index on (user_id, email_hash) WHERE email_hash IS NOT NULL prevents duplicates
leads gains contact_id (FK, nullable) and email_hash; lead_activities gains contact_id (nullable) so a timeline can span every inquiry from the same person; the auto-log triggers populate it

submit-lead finds-or-creates the contact by (user_id, email_hash), falling back to phone_hash, sets leads.contact_id, and records the inquiry on the contact timeline; a returning person produces one contact with two leads, verified by a test that submits twice with the same email and different casing/whitespace

A service-role backfill function on the pattern of backfill-lead-pii decrypts existing leads, hashes, and creates one contact per (user_id, email) with stage derived from the best lead status (converted -> past_client, otherwise lead); it is idempotent and reports counts

personal_details is bounded like form_data (max keys, key and value length, no nested objects) in the edge function that writes it, and its allowed keys are documented (partner_name, children, pets, employer, interests, notes)

src/integrations/supabase/types.ts is regenerated; npm run verify:schema passes with the new tables (RLS on, no unconditional anon policy, SECURITY DEFINER functions pin search_path); npm run test:run and tsc pass

userStories.title: The lead detail hides most of what the form captured, and the CRM overflows on a phone
userStories.description: The public forms capture more than the CRM shows. splitFormData lifts price_range, timeline, property_address, preapproved and message into columns (src/lib/leadSubmission.ts:79-117); everything else — buyer propertyType, bedrooms, preApprovalStatus; seller bathrooms, reason; valuation squareFeet, yearBuilt, condition — lands in form_data, and the only key ever read back is budget (src/components/leads/LeadDetailModal.tsx:63-65, 504-510). leads.listing_id is written at capture (leadSubmission.ts:138) and never rendered: the modal shows property_address text only (LeadDetailModal.tsx:497-503), so 'which listing did they ask about', the point of US-096, is invisible. userStories.title: Buyer and seller pipelines: a deal record with stages, not a lead with a status
userStories.description: After a lead is marked converted the product has nothing more to say. buildLeadStatusPatch sets closed_at (src/lib/leadStatus.ts:21-77) and that is the end: no transaction record, no stage between 'qualified' and 'converted', no link to the property, no expected close date, no price, no side. A buyer touring homes for four months and a seller waiting on a listing appointment are both 'qualified'. The user asked for full management of prospects for buying and selling; that is a pipeline per side with stages an agent recognises, and it needs its own record because one person can be buying and selling at once.

userStories.title: Closing a deal turns a prospect into a past client, with the dates that matter already filled in
userStories.description: Nothing happens when a deal closes. Today 'converted' sets closed_at and getLeadNextStep suggests a check-in whose button prefills a task seven days out (src/lib/leadNextStep.ts:68-75, LeadDetailModal.tsx:242-249). There is no record of what was bought or sold, at what price, on what date, or where the person now lives — which is exactly the data that drives the home-anniversary card, the annual equity check-in, and the referral ask. Sold listings are edited by hand on the Listings page (status 'sold', sold_date) with no link to the client. The review page has existed at /:username/review since US-074, but nothing asks a client to use it at the moment they are happiest.

Overview shows 'Closed this year' (count and volume from deals) and the People page shows past clients sorted by closing date
A test covers each side of the close and the anniversary row; tsc, lint and test:run pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Depends on US-131. This is the bridge between the prospect half and the relationship half of the product. Do not create testimonials automatically — the client writes the review, the agent moderates it (US-074).

userStories.title: Birthdays, home anniversaries and due tasks reach the agent — by email, in a morning digest, not only if they open the dashboard
userStories.description: The hourly job (supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/index.ts, .github/workflows/scheduled-maintenance.yml) chases only unanswered new leads past sla_hours (:74-169). Due follow-up tasks are visible solely in DueFollowUps on Overview (src/components/dashboard/DueFollowUps.tsx, useDueLeadTasks) — nothing server-side reads task_due_date, so an agent who does not log in that morning is never reminded. There are no date fields to remind about at all (US-128 adds them). notify-lead sends instantly for agents who chose daily_digest 'because no digest job exists' (supabase/functions/notify-lead/index.ts:109-114). profiles has no timezone column, so 'morning' cannot be computed. The reminder engine the user described — birthdays, closing anniversaries, important dates, with enough notice to send a card — can ship on the existing job, the notifications table and _shared/email.ts with no new infrastructure; the overdue_leads task is the pattern (per-agent preferences, at-most-once dedupe through notifications.data).
acceptanceCriteria: profiles gains timezone (IANA name, default America/New_York, set from the browser on first dashboard load and editable in Settings) and notification_preferences gains dates (instant|digest|off), digest_hour (0-23, default 7) and reminder_days_before (default 7)

scheduled-maintenance gains an upcoming_dates task: for every contacts.birthday and contact_important_dates row whose next occurrence is exactly reminder_days_before days away or today (in the agent's timezone; 29 February observed on 28 February in non-leap years), insert a notifications row of type important_date with data {contact_id, date_id, occurrence: 'YYYY'} at most once per occurrence, and email the agent when dates is instant

scheduled-maintenance gains a daily_digest task that runs once per agent per day at digest_hour in their timezone and sends one email with: new leads since the last digest, tasks due today and overdue, dates in the next reminder window, and (after US-134) overdue touches; agents on leads=daily_digest stop receiving instant lead emails and the comment in notify-lead is removed; an agent with nothing to report gets no email

Overview gains a 'Coming up' block listing the next 14 days of dates with the person's name, the occasion and one-tap call / text / send-a-note actions that log a touch (send-a-note is a mailto with a prefilled message until US-135, then the client email path); the block renders nothing when empty like DueFollowUps
Tapping an important_date notification opens the contact drawer (notification-dropdown.tsx deep link, like lead_overdue)

Unit tests cover next-occurrence maths (year rollover, leap day, timezone day boundary) and the once-per-occurrence dedupe; the job SQL is exercised against a real Postgres like US-103; tsc, lint and test:run pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Depends on US-128 for the date rows; the digest and task-reminder halves do not and can ship first. GitHub Actions cron is hourly at :17; a digest_hour is therefore honoured to the hour, which is fine. This is the highest-value story in the batch per unit of work: it is what makes the imported past-client list (US-129) do something the week it is imported.

userStories.title: Stay-in-touch cadence and referral tracking, so past clients are never quietly forgotten
userStories.description: Nothing measures time since the agent last spoke to a person: contacted_at records first contact only (src/lib/leadStatus.ts:70-73), and after that a lead can sit untouched forever with no signal. Referrals — the reason to stay in touch — are untracked: source 'referral' is a scoring weight (src/lib/ml-lead-scoring.ts:119, lead-scoring.ts:249) that no code ever writes, the public forms never ask how the person found the agent, and there is no referred_by anywhere. The nav description for Workflows promises 'Automate follow-up when a lead arrives'; the follow-up that keeps a past client sending business is a call every quarter, and the product cannot tell an agent who is due one.
acceptanceCriteria: contacts gains touch_cadence_days (nullable); Settings holds per-stage defaults (past_client 90, sphere 60, active_buyer 7, active_seller 7; leads use sla_hours instead); a trigger recomputes next_touch_at from last_contacted_at + effective cadence whenever either changes

A trigger on lead_activities sets contacts.last_contacted_at on any call, sms, email, meeting or note by the agent (is_internal notes count; automated emails do not), including activities on leads linked to the contact

The People page has an 'Overdue' filter (next_touch_at < now) and Overview shows a 'Reach out' block of the five most overdue people with call / text / email actions that log the touch and clear the overdue state; the daily digest (US-133) includes the count

The four public forms and the open-house sign-in gain an optional 'How did you hear about me?' select (Instagram, Facebook, Google, Zillow, Realtor.com, Referral, Open house, Yard sign, Other) that writes leads.source with the values scoring already knows (src/lib/ml-lead-scoring.ts:118-128) and, for Referral, a free-text referrer name into form_data.referrer_name
referred_by_contact_id is editable in the contact drawer with a contact picker; a contact shows how many people they referred and who; Analytics gains leads-by-source from real data
Tests cover the cadence trigger and the referral field; tsc, lint and test:run pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Depends on US-128 and US-129. Keep the cadence defaults editable but not the stage list.

userStories.title: Email to clients in the agent’s name, with consent, an unsubscribe link and a suppression list
userStories.description: Every email the platform sends is from one global FROM_EMAIL, default noreply@agentbio.net (supabase/functions/_shared/email.ts:51-71); nothing reads a per-agent sender, and agent-contact.ts resolves the agent only as a recipient. That is fine for alerts to the agent and not fine for a birthday note, a listing match or an open-house thank-you to a client. There is no unsubscribe: one hardcoded ${SITE_URL}/unsubscribe link (send-listing-generator-email/index.ts:282) and an {{unsubscribe_url}} placeholder (src/lib/instagram-bio-analyzer/email-templates.ts:440) point at a route that does not exist; there is no suppression table, no List-Unsubscribe header, no bounce or complaint handling, and the privacy policy promises all of it (src/pages/legal/PrivacyPolicy.tsx:184-196). No public form records consent. createAutoResponseEmail (email.ts:177) has zero callers. Every client-facing story in this batch (US-130, 132, 133, 136, 138, 139, 140) needs this first, and CAN-SPAM requires the sender's postal address, which profiles does not hold.
acceptanceCriteria: _shared/email.ts gains sendClientEmail({ agentUserId, contactId, to, subject, html, text, category: 'transactional'|'marketing' }): From is '<agent full_name> via AgentBio <agents@agentbio.net>' (or the configured client-sending domain), Reply-To is the agent's auth email, the footer carries agent name, brokerage, licence, the agent's postal address and an unsubscribe link, and List-Unsubscribe / List-Unsubscribe-Post headers are set

profiles gains office_address (required before the first marketing email; Settings explains why); sendClientEmail refuses marketing email while it is blank, and refuses any email to a contact with do_not_contact, an email_suppressions row, or (for marketing) email_opt_in false, returning {ok:false, reason}

Migration creates email_suppressions (user_id nullable for global, email_hash, reason CHECK IN (unsubscribe, bounce, complaint, manual), created_at) with RLS; a public /unsubscribe/:token route (token = HMAC of contact_id + user_id + purpose, verified in an edge function) confirms in one tap, writes the suppression, sets contacts.email_opt_in false and logs it on the timeline

A resend-webhook edge function verifies the Resend signature (pattern of _shared/webhook-auth.ts) and handles email.bounced and email.complained by writing a global suppression, and email.delivered/opened/clicked by updating the matching lead_activities metadata (which is what the email_opened and email_clicked workflow triggers will read)
Every sendClientEmail call writes a lead_activities row (activity_type email, is_internal false, metadata.provider_id) so the contact timeline is the audit trail
The four public forms and the open-house sign-in carry a consent line and checkbox that sets contacts.email_opt_in (transactional replies to the inquiry itself do not need it; sequences and notes do)
The privacy policy text matches what is built; email.test.ts covers the refusal paths and the header set; tsc, lint and test:run pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Depends on US-128 for email_hash and email_opt_in. Sending from the platform domain with the agent as Reply-To avoids per-agent domain verification entirely; note in docs/deploy which Resend domain and webhook secret the environment needs (names only, never values). Do the suppression list before any story sends its first marketing email.

userStories.title: Follow-up sequences that actually run: a durable step queue, a send_email node that sends, and seeded templates
userStories.description: The workflow builder is a complete UI with no runtime. execute-workflow has zero callers in src/ (the builder's run button calls start_workflow_execution, which only inserts a workflow_executions row — src/stores/useWorkflowBuilderStore.ts:684). Its send_email node console.logs and returns {success:true, sentAt} without importing _shared/email.ts (supabase/functions/execute-workflow/index.ts:37-53); its delay node is an in-process setTimeout capped at 5000 ms 'for testing' (:210-225), so a 'wait 2 days' step cannot exist. workflow_triggers accepts lead_created and thirteen other types that nothing dispatches; get_scheduled_workflows and workflow_execution_queue (with scheduled_for and locked_at indexes) exist with no caller. workflow_templates and workflow_node_templates have zero seed rows. pricing-plans.ts sells followUpSequences on every paid tier and Overview.tsx:94 lists 'Follow-up sequences' as a plan feature. Separately, the two lead-magnet drips (send-scheduled-listing-emails, send-scheduled-bio-emails) send email 1 from the tool pages and never emails 2-7, because no cron calls them.
acceptanceCriteria: submit-lead (after the contact upsert), the deal stage-change path and the open-house sign-in enqueue a workflow_executions row plus the first workflow_execution_queue step for each of the agent’s active, published workflows whose trigger matches (lead_created, lead_status_changed, deal_stage_changed, open_house_checkin); the dispatch is one shared helper in _shared

scheduled-maintenance gains a workflow_queue task that claims due steps (scheduled_for <= now, locked_at IS NULL) through a FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED RPC, runs each through execute-workflow, records the step in workflow_execution_steps, and on a delay node writes scheduled_for = now + delay and returns; a step that throws is retried up to three times then marks the execution failed; the claim is idempotent under two concurrent runs (tested)

send_email uses sendClientEmail (US-135) with {{first_name}}, {{agent_name}}, {{listing_address}} and {{open_house_address}} substitution and refuses without consent; create_task, update_lead and webhook_call keep working; a node type the executor does not implement cannot be published

workflow_templates is seeded with four real sequences — New buyer inquiry (5 touches over 14 days), New seller inquiry (4 touches), Open house follow-up (thank-you at +1 h, still-interested at +2 days, market update at +14 days), Past client annual check-in — and WorkflowsListPage offers 'Start from a template'

subscription_plans gains max_active_workflows (free 1, starter 3, professional 10, team/enterprise unlimited) enforced by enforce_plan_limit on publish; the Overview and Subscription feature rows read it
The two lead-magnet sequences are either driven from the same queue task (emails 2-7 send) or deleted with their tables — decision recorded in the notes
A workflow execution is visible on the contact timeline (one activity per sent email or created task, referencing the workflow); tsc, lint, test:run and verify:schema pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Depends on US-128 and US-135. Do not build a second scheduler: the hourly GitHub Actions cron and scheduled-maintenance are the clock (US-103), so step timing is honoured to the hour; anything that must be immediate (the open-house thank-you) is sent synchronously by the function that handles the event, not by a workflow. If hourly proves too coarse, tighten the cron, do not add pg_cron.

userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Independent of the contacts work; the sign-in itself is US-138. The status field is derived (scheduled/live/ended) from the times except for cancelled.

userStories.title: Open-house sign-in: a kiosk page guests use on the agent’s tablet, a live guest list, and a thank-you that goes out before they reach the car
userStories.description: There is no sign-in sheet, kiosk, guest registration or check-in of any kind in src/ (zero hits). docs/product/features.md:2017-2120 specced one in 2025 — kiosk mode, qualifying questions, consent, instant confirmation, automated follow-up — and none of it was built. The user named this as the first of the things people don't think about: a paper sheet loses the guest, and the guest who signed in and never heard back is the deal that went to the other agent. The pieces now exist to do it properly: submit-lead encrypts and rate-limits, US-128 turns a guest into a contact, US-135 can send in the agent's name, US-136 can follow up on a schedule, US-137 gives the event a code.
acceptanceCriteria: Public route /:username/oh/:code renders a full-screen, tablet-first kiosk: a welcome screen with the listing photo and agent, 'Tap to sign in', a form (name required; email or phone required; the optional questions the event enabled: working with an agent?, pre-approved?, timeframe 0-3/3-6/6-12/12+ months; a consent checkbox with the copy from US-135), a thank-you screen that returns to welcome after 8 seconds; 44px targets, no dashboard chrome, no navigation away; the question set is fixed and contains nothing about a protected class (documented in the component)
Sign-ins are queued in IndexedDB (src/lib/offline-storage.ts) and flushed on reconnect, so a venue with bad signal loses nobody; a small 'N pending' indicator shows the agent the queue is draining

submit-lead accepts lead_type 'open_house' with open_house_id: it checks the code is live (starts_at − 2 h to ends_at + 2 h), rate-limits per event through check_rate_limit, upserts the contact (US-128), inserts the lead with source 'open_house' and listing_id, inserts an open_house_signins row (open_house_id, contact_id, lead_id, answers jsonb, signed_in_at) and increments guest_count

Immediately after sign-in the guest receives a transactional thank-you through sendClientEmail with the listing link, three photos and the agent’s contact details; if the agent has the seeded Open house follow-up workflow active, US-136 enqueues it

The agent's phone shows the live guest list for the event (Supabase realtime on open_house_signins) with tap-to-call and tap-to-text that log a touch; after the event a Follow up checklist marks each guest contacted, and the event page shows a report: guests, opt-ins, contacted %, deals started
The lead scoring source weights include open_house; the Leads inbox shows the event on the card; the kiosk page emits no analytics view against the agent’s profile counters
Playwright covers the kiosk loop at a 768×1024 viewport and the offline queue; unit tests cover code validity and the consent gate; tsc, lint and test:run pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-03 product deep-dive (docs/reviews/PRODUCT_REVIEW_2026-09-03.md). Depends on US-128, US-135, US-137; the follow-up sequence needs US-136. The thank-you is sent synchronously by submit-lead, not by a workflow, because the hourly clock is too slow for it. Keep the kiosk a separate lazy route so its bundle is small and it loads fast on a tablet.

userStories.title: Buyer criteria on the person, and “3 buyers match this listing” when a listing is added
userStories.description: The buyer form captures price range, timeline, bedrooms, property type and pre-approval (src/components/forms/BuyerInquiryForm.tsx:77-86), and after US-130 the agent can at least read them. Nothing uses them: there is no place to keep a buyer's criteria as they sharpen over a few showings, and adding a listing does not tell the agent which of their own buyers it suits. The scoring inputs listingViews and hasViewedMultipleListings are never measured (src/lib/lead-scoring.ts:138-145). Matching an agent's active buyers to their new listing is the everyday win of a CRM that knows both sides, and it is a query, not a model.
acceptanceCriteria: deals (buy side) gains buyer_criteria jsonb {price_min, price_max, beds_min, baths_min, property_types[], areas[] (cities or zips), must_haves text}, prefilled from the originating lead’s price_range and form_data on Start a deal, and editable in the deal card and contact drawer

A SQL function match_buyers_for_listing(listing_id) returns the agent’s open buy-side deals whose criteria the listing satisfies (price within range, beds/baths at least, property type in list, city or zip in areas; empty criteria fields match anything); the inverse match_listings_for_deal(deal_id) returns the agent’s own active listings for a buyer
After Add or Edit listing the dashboard shows 'N buyers match' with a link; the Listings card carries the count; the deal card and contact drawer show 'Matches' from the agent's active listings

'Send to matching buyers' previews and sends one listing email per matching contact through sendClientEmail (marketing category, consent required), logs an activity per contact, and never sends the same listing to the same contact twice
Tests cover the matcher against a seeded set (price boundaries, empty criteria, area by zip); tsc, lint, test:run and verify:schema pass

userStories.title: Appointments: showings and consultations on a calendar the agent and the client both receive
